**Dimension calculation improvements:**

* Updated the `Board` component in `Board.ts` to only compute `width` and `height` from the outline if those properties are not explicitly provided. This prevents accidental overriding of user-specified dimensions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-997caa59e02ce9b6365701e5dc6954dfb1fa19b8247273d517445138af9b4b68L409-R409) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-997caa59e02ce9b6365701e5dc6954dfb1fa19b8247273d517445138af9b4b68R419-R426)

**Testing:**

* Added a new test `board-outline-with-dimensions.test.tsx` to confirm that explicit `width` and `height` are used when both dimensions and an outline are present.

Implements export functionality for tournament standings to CSV and JSON formats, with architecture designed for adding PDF, Excel, and other formats.

## Changes

**Export Service** (`lib/services/export_service.dart`)
- Strategy pattern implementation for extensible format support
- CSV export: all player statistics in spreadsheet-ready format
- JSON export: tournament metadata + complete standings with calculated metrics
- Filename sanitization handling edge cases (empty names, special chars, consecutive spaces)

**UI Integration**
- Export dialog (`lib/widgets/export_dialog.dart`) with format selection
- Download buttons on Tournament Completion and Leaderboard screens
- Platform-aware file download (web via conditional imports, mobile shows not-yet-implemented message)
- Info dialog documenting planned export formats

**Data Exported**
- Rankings, points, wins/losses, matches played, win rate %
- Biggest win/smallest loss margins, pause count

**Code Quality**
- `Constants.noLossesSentinel` replaces magic number 999
- 15+ unit tests covering CSV/JSON generation, filename sanitization edge cases
- Platform compatibility stub (`lib/utils/html_stub.dart`) for cross-platform builds

## Example Usage

```dart
final csvData = ExportService.exportStandings(
  standings: standings,
  tournament: tournament,
  format: ExportFormat.csv,
);
// Returns: "Rank,Player Name,Total Points,Wins,Losses,..."
```

Adding new formats requires implementing `ExportStrategy` interface:

```dart
class PdfExportStrategy implements ExportStrategy {
  @override
  String get fileExtension => 'pdf';
  
  @override
  String exportStandings(List<PlayerStanding> standings, Tournament tournament) {
    // PDF generation logic
  }
}
```

### Motivation
- Improve readability and teaching value of the code by adding short, descriptive inline comments to each executable line in the `lperfect` package.
- Make control flow, assignments, imports, and API entry points easier to scan for newcomers and code reviewers.
- Preserve existing docstrings and keep all runtime behavior unchanged.
- Provide a uniform commenting convention across the package to aid maintenance.

### Description
- Added concise trailing comments to executable lines across all `lperfect/*.py` modules (annotations applied to imports, `def`/`class` lines, assignments, control structures, and returns).
- Preserved existing docstrings and did not modify function signatures, logic, or types; changes are comment-only.
- The commenting follows a simple pattern (e.g., `# import ...`, `# define function ...`, `# return ...`, `# check condition ...`) to keep annotations consistent.
- Changes touch all modules under `lperfect` (pedagogical annotations added throughout the package, ~16 files, ~1.2k trailing comments).

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this PR (comment-only edits).
- Because this is non-functional comment-only work, runtime behavior and test outcomes are expected to be unchanged, but no tests were run to confirm.

- Fixed `aria-hidden` prop type from string to boolean (5 instances)
- Added null coalescing for `error.stack` and `errorInfo.componentStack`
- Extended `ActivityLogEntry` interface with missing `changes` property

**Control flow**
- Fixed missing return paths in `useEffect` hooks (6 instances)
```typescript
// Before
useEffect(() => {
  if (condition) {
    return cleanup;
  }
}, [deps]);

// After
useEffect(() => {
  if (!condition) return;
  return cleanup;
}, [deps]);
```

**Code hygiene**
- Removed 30+ unused imports and variables
- Fixed timer types: `NodeJS.Timeout` → `number` for browser compatibility
- Simplified `BulkActions` by removing unused generic constraint
- Exported unused type declarations (`KPIData`, `ChartData`, `TimeSlot`)

author: copilot
body:
Complete rewrite implementing n8n webhook integration for AI chat with UUID-based session management and conversation persistence. Removes all authentication logic to provide a seamless single-page chat experience with multi-language support. ## Changes **Removed:** - All authentication modals and sign-in/sign-up logic (HTML, JavaScript, CSS) - Session/Sign In button from header - Authentication-related code (~450 lines removed) **Added:** - n8n webhook integration for AI chat responses (production endpoint) - **UUID-based session management** with user_id, chat_id, and message_id - Cryptographically secure UUID generation using crypto.randomUUID() with fallback - Conversation history management with auto-save - "Welcome Back" feature for returning users - "New Chat" button to start fresh conversations - **Language selector functionality** - supports 6 languages (English, Arabic, Russian, Chinese, Hindi, Urdu) - **SVG logo support** - updated from PNG to SVG format - **Nested response format parsing** - handles complex n8n response structures - Typing indicator animation for better UX - README.md with n8n integration guide **Fixed:** - Removed `min-height: 100vh` from `.canvas` to eliminate scroll-within-scroll - Updated deprecated `substr()` to `substring()` - Added null checks for DOM elements - Cleaned up corrupted CSS comments - **Language selector now fully functional** - saves preference to localStorage and persists across sessions ## Architecture **UUID-Based Session Management:** - **user_id**: Persistent UUID for each user, generated once and stored in localStorage (`oqta_user_id`) - **chat_id**: Unique UUID per conversation, stored in localStorage (`oqta_chat_id`), regenerated on "New Chat" - **message_id**: Unique UUID generated for each message sent - **session_id**: Legacy identifier maintained for compatibility (`oqta_session_id`) - Cryptographically secure UUID generation using native `crypto.randomUUID()` with fallback **Conversation Storage:** - All messages saved locally in `oqta_conversation` - Includes role, content, and timestamp for each message - Auto-loads on return visits **Language Support:** - Selected language saved to localStorage as `oqta_language` - Preference persists across sessions - Supports 6 languages with easy expansion **n8n Communication:** - Production webhook: `https://lemzakov.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/44d1ca27-d30f-4088-841b-0853846bb000` - POST requests to webhook with: ```json { "systemPrompt": "user message", "user_id": "uuid-v4-here", "user_email": "guest@oqta.ai", "user_name": "Guest User", "user_role": "user", "chat_id": "uuid-v4-here", "message_id": "uuid-v4-here", "chatInput": "user message" } ``` - Expected response format (nested structure): ```json { "response": { "body": { "output": "AI assistant's response here" }, "headers": {}, "statusCode": 200 } } ``` - Also supports alternative formats: `{"response": "msg"}`, `{"message": "msg"}`, `{"output": "msg"}` ## User Flow **First-time User:** 1. Lands on homepage with registration information 2. Types message and clicks send 3. Conversation area appears instantly 4. No authentication required 5. Unique user_id and chat_id automatically generated **Returning User:** 1. Page loads directly to conversation area 2. Shows "Welcome Back!" message for 3 seconds 3. Previous conversation auto-loaded 4. Language preference restored 5. Same user_id persists, can continue chatting or start new conversation (new chat_id) ## Screenshots **New User - Landing Page:** **Conversation Area:** **Welcome Back (Returning User):** **Language Selector Working:** **Mobile Responsive:** ## Configuration The n8n webhook URL is configured in `script.js`. To use a different endpoint, update the `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL` constant. Current production endpoint: `https://lemzakov.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/44d1ca27-d30f-4088-841b-0853846bb000` See README.md for complete n8n request/response format and integration setup instructions.
Original prompt > canvas area created a scrol within a scroll in html, resolve it, it should be clean responsive page. When page loads when existing user session found you should show instead of text area the conversation area not in popup. Button sign in/up should be removed. Just chat in the same area.

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive automated testing infrastructure for the critic-markup Quarto extension, adds extensive documentation for testing, and enhances the customization and documentation of DOCX markup color and formatting options. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Automated Testing Infrastructure:**

* Added a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) that runs unit tests, integration tests, and Lua code linting on every push or pull request, ensuring continuous integration and code quality.
* Introduced a `Makefile` with commands for running tests, installing dependencies, linting, and cleaning up test artifacts, making local testing and development easier.

**Testing Documentation:**

* Added a new `TESTING.md` file that details the testing setup, instructions for running and adding tests, troubleshooting, and coverage information.
* Updated `README.md` with a new "Testing" section summarizing test types, quick start instructions, and a reference to `TESTING.md`.

**DOCX Markup Customization and Documentation:**

* Expanded `README.md` with detailed instructions and examples for customizing DOCX markup colors and formatting, including options for colored backgrounds (`docx-color`), simple markup styles (`docx-simple-markup`), and custom color overrides. body:
Creates standard Unix man page documentation for gogrep command-line tool.

## Changes

- **gogrep.1**: 193-line man page in groff format with 14 sections
  - Complete command syntax, options, and examples
  - Regex pattern reference (RE2 syntax)
  - Supported file types (ZIP, TAR.GZ, XLSX, text)
  - Performance characteristics and concurrency notes
  - Accurate flag status: `-count` and `-ignore-case` are parsed but not implemented
  - Workaround for case-insensitive search using `(?i)` regex prefix

- **README.md**: Installation instructions for viewing/installing man page

## Flag Implementation Status

Working flags documented as-is:
- `-color`: Colorized output (default on Linux)
- `-mask`: File pattern filtering within archives
- `-num-worker`: Concurrent worker count

Non-functional flags documented with clear notes:
- `-count`: Accepted but no effect on behavior
- `-ignore-case`: Not implemented; use `(?i)` prefix in pattern instead

## Usage

```bash
# View locally
man ./gogrep.1

# Install system-wide
sudo cp gogrep.1 /usr/local/share/man/man1/
sudo mandb
```

author: ajfafg
body:
## Background

When an HTTP response was in the 3xx series, this rule previously sent an HTTP request to the Location header value. Consequently, when the Location header value was a relative path, the HTTP request was not sent to the expected URI.

## Approach

I modified the behavior to resolve the URI in the Location header value using the origin of the URI that sent the initial HTTP request. Additionally, to demonstrate that this change works as expected, I added an implementation on the test server and corresponding test cases.

author: copilot
body:
The workflow used `tj-actions/coverage-badge-js@v1` which expects `coverage-summary.json`, but Bun's test runner only generates LCOV format.

## Changes

- **Test command**: Added `--coverage-reporter=lcov --coverage-dir=./coverage` flags to generate LCOV output
- **Badge generation**: Replaced GitHub Action with shell script that:
  - Parses LCOV DA records (`DA:<line_number>,<execution_count>`) via awk
  - Calculates coverage using floating-point arithmetic: `(covered * 100.0) / total`
  - Validates coverage value with regex and color against whitelist
  - Generates badge via shields.io API with HTTP status checking
  - Color thresholds: ≥80% brightgreen, ≥60% green, ≥40% yellow, ≥20% orange, <20% red

```yaml
# Extract coverage from LCOV format
COVERAGE=$(awk '
  /^DA:/ { 
    split($0, parts, ":")
    split(parts[2], counts, ",")
    total++
    if (counts[2] > 0) covered++
  }
  END { 
    if (total > 0) {
      pct = (covered * 100.0) / total
      printf "%.1f", pct
    } else {
      print "0.0"
    }
  }
' ./coverage/lcov.info)
```

## Security

- Input validation prevents injection via regex pattern matching
- Color value validated against whitelist before URL construction
- HTTP status code checked before accepting badge file
- CodeQL scan: 0 alerts

author: matejskultety
body:
This pull request introduces a major restructuring of the project's container orchestration setup. The previous `docker-compose.yml` file has been removed and replaced by a new, more modular `docker-compose.yaml` that uses YAML anchors for reusable configurations, introduces a reverse proxy service, and unifies network management. Additionally, the `.devcontainer` configuration has been updated to forward ports that match the new setup.

**Container orchestration and configuration overhaul:**

* Introduced a new `docker-compose.yaml` file that uses YAML anchors for reusable configuration blocks, improving maintainability and reducing duplication. The new file defines separate services for backend, frontend, and a reverse proxy, and organizes them under a single custom bridge network.
* Removed the old `docker-compose.yml` file, which previously defined backend, frontend, and database services, along with their volumes and dependencies.

**Service architecture improvements:**

* Added a `reverse-proxy` service (using Nginx) to handle frontend routing and expose only necessary ports, enhancing security and flexibility.
* Updated port forwarding in `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` to match the new service ports (80 and 8080 instead of 3000 and 8000), aligning the development environment with the new architecture.

4. **Commented out binary-only visualizations:**
   - scoremodelplot() functions (threshold-based TP/FP/TN/FN categorization)
   - younden() threshold optimization (binary only)
   - These visualizations are incompatible with multi-class

## Changes in global.R:

1. **Removed forced binary labels:**
   - Removed names(lev)<-c("positif","negatif") (line 1652)

2. **Removed binary threshold optimization (lines 3343-3419):**
   - Removed Youden and equiprobability threshold methods
   - Removed ifelse() threshold-based predictions
   - Multi-class uses argmax on probability matrices (no threshold)

3. **Fixed testparametersfunction metrics:**
   - Set threshold column to NA (no threshold for multi-class)
   - Use calculate_multiclass_auc() for AUC calculations
   - Extract $macro_average from sensibility/specificity results

## Impact:

- All models now use consistent multi-class logic (argmax predictions)
- No threshold-based decision making
- Metrics use macro-averaging across all classes
- Binary visualizations removed (ROC curves provide multi-class visualization)

Resolves binary-specific code inconsistencies identified in systematic review.

body:
## Summary
Define the KalypsoTritonServer CRD for deploying NVIDIA Triton Inference Servers.

## Changes
- Define `KalypsoTritonServerSpec` with:
  - `applicationRef`: Reference to parent KalypsoApplication (required)
  - `storageUri`: S3/GCS path to model repository (required)
  - `tritonConfig`: Triton server configuration
  - `replicas`: Number of replicas (default: 1)
  - `resources`: K8s resource requests/limits
  - `networking`: Service port configuration

- Define `TritonConfigSpec` with:
  - `image`: Triton container image (default: nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver)
  - `tag`: Image tag
  - `parameters`: Triton runtime parameters
  - `backendType`: Backend type (python, tensorflow, pytorch, etc.)
  - `python_backend`: Python backend specific settings

- Define `PythonBackendSpec` with:
  - `shmDefaultByteSize`: Shared memory size in bytes
  - `extraArgs`: Additional args passed to model initialize()

- Define `NetworkingSpec` with:
  - `httpPort`: HTTP port (default: 8000)
  - `grpcPort`: gRPC port (default: 8001)
  - `metricsPort`: Metrics port (default: 8002)

- Define `KalypsoTritonServerStatus` with:
  - `phase`: Current phase (Pending, Running, Failed)
  - `deploymentName`: Name of created K8s Deployment
  - `serviceEndpoint`: Service endpoint URL
  - `availableReplicas`: Number of available replicas
  - `message`: Human-readable status message

- Add scale subresource for HPA support
- Add printcolumns for Application, Phase, Replicas, Available, Age
- Add sample CR for KalypsoTritonServer

Closes #6

Closes https://github.com/portfolio-performance/portfolio/issues/2490
Closes https://github.com/portfolio-performance/portfolio/issues/4063

Hello, on the Securities Chart, when you hit the '0' accelerator key or trigger the 'reset to Original size' action, the graph becomes incorrect when there are the positive/négative area on it.
What I understand : 
* SecuritiesChart is a TimelineChart and therefore the adjustRange of Timelinechart is used for those actions
* However In the updateChart of SecuritiesCharts, dedicated ranges are used for yAxis2nd and yAxis3rd, so if adjustRange is called after, the particular settings is lost.

So what I propose is to call updateChart at the end of the adjustRange method of timelinechart. But this means changing from private to public. I think this works. Otherwise, at first I was thinking we could get an override adjustRange method for SecuritiesCharts, but this was not so straightforward.

~~While I write this, I note that I did not check the behaviour when multiple securities are selected, I will check.~~
-> OK, no problem seen with multi securities selection.

body: **Your checklist for this pull request** - [X] I've read the [guidelines for contributing](https://github.com/rizinorg/rizin/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md) to this repository. - [X] I made sure to follow the project's [coding style](https://github.com/rizinorg/rizin/blob/dev/DEVELOPERS.md#code-style). - [X] I've documented every `RZ_API` function and struct this PR changes. - [X] I've added tests that prove my changes are effective (required for changes to `RZ_API`). - [ ] I've updated the [Rizin book](https://github.com/rizinorg/book) with the relevant information (if needed). - [ ] I've used AI tools to generate fully or partially these code changes and I'm sure the changes are not copyrighted by somebody else. **Detailed description** When targeting ARM (Thumb-1 mode) and optimizing for size, GCC uses a runtime helper function `__gnu_thumb1_case_uqi` for jumping to switch case blocks. Currently the analysis code considers `bl __gnu_thumb1_case_uqi` as a standard function call and therefore skips analysis/indexing of basic blocks corresponding to the referenced switch cases. This PR adds analysis support for that kind of jump table which allows analyzing the case-related basic blocks. Regarding https://github.com/rizinorg/rizin/issues/3568 - there are no refline glitches after indexing all of the function's basic blocks although the refline glitch itself is probably a separate issue, not fixed by this PR. The glitch can still be reproduced if `e analysis.jmp.tbl=false` is set before analysis. body:
Projenin güncel teknik mimarisini ve tamamlanan özelliklerini kapsayan detaylı durum raporu aşağıdadır:

🏗️ Proje Mimari & Durum Raporu (Web Şube v2.0)
1. Teknik Mimari
Proje, güvenli ve modüler bir yapı sağlamak amacıyla ASP.NET Core 8 (Razor Pages) altyapısında geliştirilmiştir. "Frontend" ve "Backend" ayrımı şu prensiplere dayanır:

Backend (ASP.NET Core): Güvenlik kapısı olarak çalışır. Tarayıcıdan gelen istekleri karşılar, hassas API anahtarlarını (Secrets) saklar ve Azure Functions üzerindeki dış servislere proxy (köprü) görevi görür.
Frontend (Razor & JS): Kullanıcı deneyimini yönetir. Sayfa yenilenmeden işlem yapmak için modern Fetch API/AJAX yapısını kullanır. Tasarımda CSS Grid & Flexbox kullanılarak "Responsive" (Her cihaza uyumlu) bir yapı kurulmuştur.
2. Tamamlanan Modüller & Özellikler
A. Kimlik Doğrulama (Authentication Flow) 🔐
Kullanıcının sisteme güvenli giriş yapmasını sağlayan modüldür.

Akış: Telefon Girişi -> KVKK Onayı -> OTP (SMS) Gönderimi -> OTP Doğrulama.
Özellikler:
TCKN Tespiti: Girilen numaradan kullanıcının TCKN'sini arka planda bulur (API entegreli).
KVKK Döngüsü: Kullanıcı KVKK onayı vermemişse otomatik olarak onay popup'ı açılır.
Bypass Mekanizması: Geliştirme sürecini tıkamamak için 123456 kodu ile test girişi aktiftir.
Güvenlik: Başarılı girişte HttpOnly cookie oluşturularak oturum açılır.
B. Dashboard (Kullanıcı Paneli) 📊
Kullanıcının finansal durumunu özetleyen ana ekrandır.

Tasarım: Figma tasarımına sadık kalınarak modern, ferah ve mobil uyumlu bir arayüz kodlandı.
Bileşenler:
Sidebar (Sol Menü): Tüm modüllere (Raporlar, Faturalar, Ayarlar) erişim sağlayan, açılıp kapanabilir menü.
Kredi Skoru Kartı: Kullanıcının mevcut risk durumunu gösteren görsel gösterge (Gauge).
Aksiyon Kartı: Kullanıcıya özel tavsiyeler ve "Teklifleri Gör" butonu.
Hızlı İşlemler: Sık kullanılan özelliklere (Adres Güncelle, Rapor Gör vb.) tek tıkla erişim.
4. Entegrasyon Durumu
✅ Login API'leri: Tamamen entegre (CheckUser, KVKKonay, GenerateOTP, SendOTP, VerifyOTP).
⚠️ Dashboard Verileri: Şu an Statik (Görüntü amaçlı). "Mustafa Gümüş", Skor verisi vb. kodun içinde sabit yazılıdır. Backend API'lere bağlanarak dinamik hale getirilmesi gerekmektedir.
5. Sırada Ne Var? (Next Steps)
Dashboard API Bağlantısı: Statik verilerin (İsim, Skor, Tavsiyeler) gerçek kullanıcı verisiyle değiştirilmesi.
Sayfaların Çoğaltılması: "Rapor Detayları", "Profil Ayarları" gibi linklerin, 
Index.cshtml
 yapısı baz alınarak yeni sayfalar olarak oluşturulması.

body:
🎯 Add RAG-based Knowledge Base Management System

Team Member: Muhammad Ali (FA22-BCS-115)  
Component: Knowledge Base Management  
Internship Project: AI Voice Agent for Customer Service



 📦 What's Being Added

This PR adds the Knowledge Base Management component to our AI Voice Agent project. This component works alongside the existing codebase and handles company-specific knowledge retrieval using RAG.

 ✅ New Component Added
```
AI_voice_agent/
├── app/                           (Existing - Zeeshan's code)
├── tests/                         (Existing - Zeeshan's code)
├── knowledge-base-system/         ← NEW: My component
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py               FastAPI application
│   │   ├── config.py             Configuration
│   │   ├── core/
│   │   │   ├── embeddings.py     Embedding generation
│   │   │   ├── chunking.py       Document chunking
│   │   │   ├── retrieval.py      RAG retrieval
│   │   │   └── vector_store.py   FAISS vector store
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   └── api/
│   ├── knowledge_bases/          Sample company data
│   ├── tests/                    Test suite
│   └── requirements.txt
└── (other existing files)
```



 🎯 Features Implemented

- FAISS Vector Database - Fast semantic search with 384-dimensional embeddings
- Hybrid Chunking Strategy - Sentence-based chunking (400-500 words with overlap)
- FastAPI REST API - 8 production-ready endpoints
- Multi-Company Support - Easy switching between different company knowledge bases
- Sentence Transformers - Using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for embeddings
- Sample Data - 3 companies: TechStore, HealthPlus, EduLearn
- Comprehensive Tests - Test suite with pytest
- Complete Documentation - Setup guide, API docs



 🚀 API Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--|-|-|
| POST | `/company/load` | Load company knowledge base |
| POST | `/company/switch` | Switch active company |
| POST | `/query` | Query knowledge base |
| POST | `/context` | Get formatted context for LLM |
| GET | `/companies` | List all available companies |
| GET | `/health` | System health check |
| POST | `/ingest` | Re-ingest documents |
| DELETE | `/company/{id}` | Remove company |



 🔗 Integration with Existing Code

This component is designed to integrate seamlessly with the existing voice agent system:

 Integration Flow:
```
Call Input → STT (Existing) → My KB System → LLM → TTS (Existing) → Call Output
```

 For Other Team Members:
```python
import requests

 Get context from knowledge base
response = requests.post(
    "http://localhost:8001/context",   Different port to avoid conflict
    json={
        "company_id": "techstore",
        "query": transcribed_text
    }
)
context = response.json()["formatted_context"]

 Pass to LLM for response generation
```



 🛠️ Technical Stack

- Backend: FastAPI + Python 3.10+
- Vector DB: FAISS (IndexFlatL2)
- Embeddings: sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
- Validation: Pydantic v2
- Logging: Loguru
- Testing: Pytest



 📋 Installation & Setup
```bash
 Install dependencies for knowledge base system
cd knowledge-base-system
pip install -r requirements.txt

 Run the knowledge base service (separate from main app)
python run.py
 Service runs on http://localhost:8001 (different port)
```



 ⚡ Performance Metrics

- Query Retrieval: <200ms
- Memory Usage: ~450MB per company
- Concurrent Requests: 50+
- Retrieval Accuracy: >80% on test set



 ✅ Testing
```bash
cd knowledge-base-system
pytest tests/ -v
```

All tests passing ✅



 📝 Notes for Team

- This component runs on a separate port (8001) to avoid conflicts with existing services
- All my code is contained within the `knowledge-base-system/` folder
- No modifications made to existing files
- Ready to integrate with STT/LLM/TTS components
- Complete documentation included in the folder



 🔄 No Conflicts

This PR adds a new folder and does not modify any existing code from the main project, so there should be no merge conflicts.

2.  **Geometry:** Added Section 2 distinguishing Points (affine) vs. Vectors (linear).

2.  **Subspaces:** Added Section 2 defining subspace criteria and algebra (intersection, sum).
3.  **Basis & Dimension:** Expanded Section 3 with the Steinitz Exchange Lemma and coordinate uniqueness.
4.  **Renumbering:** Shifted Linear Maps, Eigenvalues, Induced Norms, QR, SVD, and Pseudoinverse to subsequent sections.

author: kampute
body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and updates across the codebase, focusing primarily on enhancing HTTP error handling and updating dependencies to support .NET 10.0 and newer library versions. The most significant changes are the introduction of a new abstract base class for retryable HTTP error handling and a refactor of the `HttpError429Handler` to leverage this abstraction. Additionally, there are updates to project metadata and dependency versions, as well as workflow configuration changes.

### HTTP Error Handling Improvements

* Added a new abstract base class `RetryableHttpErrorHandler` in `src/Kampute.HttpClient/ErrorHandlers/Abstracts/RetryableHttpErrorHandler.cs`, which provides a reusable mechanism for handling transient HTTP errors with customizable backoff and retry strategies. This class is designed to be extended for specific error codes and centralizes retry logic.
* Refactored `HttpError429Handler` in `src/Kampute.HttpClient/ErrorHandlers/HttpError429Handler.cs` to inherit from `RetryableHttpErrorHandler`, simplifying its implementation and aligning its retry logic with the new abstraction. The handler now uses a rate limit reset header for retry timing and disables retries if not present.
* Added a documentation-only class `NamespaceDoc` to `src/Kampute.HttpClient/ErrorHandlers/Abstracts/NamespaceDoc.cs` to clarify the purpose of the error handler abstracts namespace.

### Dependency and SDK Updates

* Updated the GitHub Actions workflow in `.github/workflows/main.yml` to use .NET SDK 10.0.x instead of 8.0.x, ensuring compatibility with the latest .NET features.
* Changed package references in project files (`Kampute.HttpClient.Json.csproj`, `Kampute.HttpClient.NewtonsoftJson.csproj`) to use wildcard versions (`10.*` for `System.Text.Json` and `13.*` for `Newtonsoft.Json`), allowing for automatic updates to the latest minor and patch releases. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2ee4ab9e1f5c14c19d8e5afe317c9396379fb3209784c6cbe0ad39d763bfd6c2L39-R39) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6215240a5f2a08d30bc9d031b739abdb968869584b36553bce92886f72cd64c0L39-R39)

### Project Metadata Updates

* Bumped package versions from `2.4.0` to `2.5.0` and updated copyright years to 2025 in `Kampute.HttpClient.DataContract.csproj`, `Kampute.HttpClient.NewtonsoftJson.csproj`, and `Kampute.HttpClient.Xml.csproj` to reflect the new release. ### Motivation
- Establish a PR-driven workflow with Confluence as the source of truth for specifications.
- Provide a GitHub Actions CI job to automatically restore, build, and test .NET code on GitHub-hosted runners.
- Provide a manual Confluence sync to generate mirrors of specs into the repository so PRs can reference authoritative content.

### Description
- Add governance and contributor guidance files: `AGENTS.md`, `RULES.md`, and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` to require `Feature-Key` and Confluence page references in PRs.
- Add folders `Docs/Migrations/` and `SpecsMirror/` with `SpecsMirror/README.md` and a migrations README, where `SpecsMirror/` is treated as generated output.
- Add CI workflow ` .github/workflows/core-ci.yml` that detects the `.NET` SDK from `global.json` (or falls back to LTS), locates a root `*.sln` or a single `*.csproj` under `src/`, and runs `dotnet restore`, `dotnet build`, and `dotnet test` with optional `dotnet format` verification. 
- Add manual Confluence sync workflow ` .github/workflows/confluence-sync.yml` that reads `CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL`, `CONFLUENCE_USER_EMAIL`, and `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN` from secrets, accepts `feature_key` and `confluence_page_id` inputs, fetches the page via the Confluence REST API, writes `SpecsMirror/<feature_key>/spec.md` and `SpecsMirror/<feature_key>/meta.json`, and uses a minimal HTML-to-markdown parser for the storage-format HTML.

- Same tarball hash for identical inputs
- Automatic dependency hash management via pre-commit hook

author: bendwyer
body:
This PR changes to the native installation for the claude-code feature. Using the npm version had a few drawbacks:

- npm dependency
- bloated dev container size
- errors and warnings despite a default installation

So, I am switching the feature back to the native install with some notable changes:

- claude install is not triggered until the container is built so that user-specific settings are applied for the dev container user (usually vscode) instead of root.
- versions are more carefully managed. If `stable` is chosen then this is respected, even after `claude install`. Previously `claude install` ran without a version switch so `latest` was always installed regardless of the desired version passed to the dev container feature.
- `claude doctor` will pass all tests now

This is, yet again, a breaking change so I am releasing it as v3.0.0. Apologies.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR addresses two security issues in `middleware-security.ts`:

1.  **Rate Limiting Cleanup**: The previous cleanup logic relied on `Date.now() % 1000 === 0`, which is unreliable and could lead to memory leaks if the condition is never met. A deterministic interval-based cleanup was implemented, along with a `MAX_MAP_SIZE` safety valve to prevent memory exhaustion (DoS risk).
2.  **XSS Detection Robustness**: The `detectSuspiciousActivity` function previously called `decodeURIComponent(url)` directly. Malformed URLs (e.g., invalid percent encoding) would throw an error and potentially crash the request handler. This call is now wrapped in a `try-catch` block, treating malformed URLs as suspicious/invalid without crashing.

Verified with a standalone script (`verify_fixes.ts`) and by manual inspection. The project build passes.

author: copilot
body:
The albion_ava cog was restricted to querying only its own guild's Portaler data. This adds multi-guild support with a simplified architecture using a global token.

## Changes

**Configuration**
- Token storage moved from per-guild to global config (bot owner only)
- Replaced `portaler_guild_id` and `subscribed_guild_ids` with `guild_ids` - a complete list of Portaler guilds to query per Discord server
- Removed per-guild token management

**Commands**
- `[p]setava token <token>` - Sets global token (was: per-guild with guild_id parameter)
- `[p]setava guilds <guild_id> ...` - Sets complete list of guilds to query (was: additive to primary guild)

**Data Fetching**
- `_fetch_all_guilds_data()` queries all configured guild IDs using the global token
- Added `_merge_all_map_data()` for O(n) merging across multiple guilds
- Duplicate connections resolved by keeping entries with newer expiry dates
- Added `_validate_guild_id()` helper for 17-20 digit snowflake validation

## Example Usage

```python
# Bot owner sets token once (DM)
[p]setava token eyJhbGci...

# Discord Server A queries three Portaler guilds
[p]setava guilds 111111111111111111 222222222222222222 333333333333333333

# Discord Server B queries different guilds
[p]setava guilds 222222222222222222 444444444444444444

# Both servers share the same token, see merged data from their configured guilds
[p]ava image
```

Each Discord server independently configures which Portaler guilds to monitor, enabling guild alliances to share connection data while maintaining flexibility.

body:
GTmetrix audit identified critical performance bottlenecks: 62% score (C grade), 3.7s LCP, 477KB payload, and multiple failed requests. Target: 90%+ score, <1.5s LCP, ~320KB payload. ## Critical Fixes ### HTTPS Redirect Middleware (-3.2s) HTTP→HTTPS 301 redirect chain added 3.2s latency. Added production middleware to handle redirects at application level: ```javascript // server.js if (isProduction) { app.use((req, res, next) => { const isSecure = req.secure || req.headers['x-forwarded-proto'] === 'https'; if (!isSecure) { return res.redirect(301, `${process.env.BASE_URL}${req.url}`); } // Handle non-www → www if BASE_URL contains www next(); }); } ``` ### CSRF Token Initialization `POST /api/metrics/track` returned 403 due to empty token sent before fetch completed. Implemented retry logic with timeout and cleanup: ```javascript (function sendPageview() { let timeoutId = null; function attemptSend() { if (window.__CSRF_TOKEN__) { fetch('/api/metrics/track', { headers: { 'X-CSRF-Token': window.__CSRF_TOKEN__ }}); } else if (Date.now() - startTime < 2000) { timeoutId = setTimeout(attemptSend, 100); } } window.addEventListener('beforeunload', () => clearTimeout(timeoutId), { once: true }); attemptSend(); })(); ``` ### Unsplash API Replacement Two Unsplash requests failing with 503. Replaced with local SVG placeholders (`/assets/images/placeholders/`). ## Asset Optimization ### Image Conversion (-173KB, 43% reduction) Converted JPEG images to WebP with fallback: - `collage-entertainment.jpg`: 201KB → 63KB WebP (68.5%) - `collage-venue.jpg`: 108KB → 62KB WebP (42.4%) - `collage-photography.jpg`: 82KB → 42KB WebP (48.8%) - `collage-catering.jpg`: 8KB → 6KB WebP (24.2%) ```html ``` ### Cache Headers Implemented tiered caching strategy: - HTML: `max-age=0, must-revalidate` - Versioned assets: `max-age=31536000, immutable` - Static assets: `max-age=604800, must-revalidate` ### Resource Hints Added DNS prefetch and preconnect for CDN/fonts, preload for critical CSS. ### JavaScript Delivery Added `defer` attribute to all non-critical scripts. ## Email Integration Simplification & Security Simplified email configuration to use **Mailgun only** as the exclusive email provider with secure environment variable handling: - Removed AWS SES integration (~100 lines) - Removed SendGrid integration (~30 lines) - Removed SMTP/nodemailer integration (~50 lines) - Updated `sendMail()` function to delegate directly to `utils/mailgun.js` - **Removed all hardcoded API keys and domains** - credentials now read from environment variables at runtime - Updated health checks and startup validation to only verify Mailgun - Configured for Railway deployment with secure environment variable handling - Added validation that fails gracefully if `MAILGUN_API_KEY` or `MAILGUN_DOMAIN` are not configured This reduces complexity, provides a single consistent email delivery method, and ensures secure credential management for production deployments. ### Railway Deployment Configuration The application now reads Mailgun credentials from environment variables configured in Railway dashboard: ```javascript const MAILGUN_API_KEY = process.env.MAILGUN_API_KEY; const MAILGUN_DOMAIN = process.env.MAILGUN_DOMAIN; // Validation in initializeMailgun() if (!MAILGUN_API_KEY || !MAILGUN_DOMAIN) { console.warn('Mailgun not configured: MAILGUN_API_KEY and MAILGUN_DOMAIN required'); return false; } ``` **Required Environment Variables in Railway:** - `MAILGUN_API_KEY` - Your Mailgun API key - `MAILGUN_DOMAIN` - Your verified Mailgun domain ## Expected Impact - **LCP**: 3.7s → ~1.5s (60% improvement) - **Page weight**: 477KB → ~304KB (36% reduction) - **Performance score**: C (62%) → A (90%+) - **Failed requests**: 0 (100% reliability) - **Codebase**: ~180 lines removed (email integrations) - **Security**: No hardcoded secrets, Railway-ready deployment ## Files Changed - `server.js` - HTTPS redirect, cache middleware, email simplification - `public/index.html` - Resource hints, picture elements, defer attributes - `public/assets/js/app.js` - CSRF retry with cleanup - `railway.json` - Production environment config - `.env.example` - Secure Mailgun configuration (no hardcoded secrets) - `utils/mailgun.js` - Environment variable handling, removed hardcoded fallbacks - `PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZATION.md` - Implementation guide Requires GTmetrix re-audit post-deployment to verify metrics. > [!WARNING] >

author: aloento
body:
### Summary

**This PR** introduces a large set of features and scaffolding to turn the Scotland Yard environment into a research-ready mechanism design and meta-learning project. It adds partial observability and belief-tracking, mechanism parameter plumbing and meta-learning hooks, population self-play utilities, OOD and exploitability evaluation tools, and a suite of unit tests and configs to run ablations and experiments.

---

### Key Changes

- **Partial observability**: `PartialObservationWrapper` that hides MrX position, supports reveal schedules, noisy hints, and injects belief maps into police observations.
- **Belief tracking**: lightweight `ParticleBeliefTracker` and a tiny `LearnedBeliefEncoder` to support both classical and learned belief representations.
- **Action masking**: deterministic fixed index to node mapping and `ActionMaskResult` utilities that enforce budget and toll constraints.
- **Mechanism design plumbing**: `MechanismConfig`, `apply_mechanism_to_env`, and a simple `MetaLearner` loop to tune mechanism parameters toward a target win rate.
- **Graph generation and OOD**: `GraphGenerator`, OOD config and evaluation utilities for graph distribution shifts, edge noise, and edge dropout robustness.
- **Population self-play**: `PopulationManager`, ELO-style scoring, best-response scaffolding, and opponent modeling utilities.
- **Exploitability and baselines**: exploitability helpers and simple heuristic MrX/Police baselines for robustness checks.
- **Evaluation metrics**: core metrics implemented (win rate, belief cross-entropy, time-to-catch) and evaluation helpers.
- **Ablation configs and runners**: Hydra-style configs for belief and mechanism ablations and an ablation runner script.
- **Tests and CI readiness**: unit tests for action mask and belief updates (`test_action_mask.py`, `test_belief_update.py`) and smoke tests.
- **Dev tooling**: WandB integration hooks, Docker snippets, and logging/metrics scaffolding.

author: iloveqyx
body:
### Motivation
- Prototype computation and class-weight estimation previously used training DataLoaders configured with `shuffle=True, drop_last=True`, causing each epoch to see a random subset and drop the last batch.
- That leads to unstable prototype banks and fluctuating pseudo-label distributions which can significantly hurt final accuracy.
- Providing full, deterministic data iteration for prototype/weight computation stabilizes statistics used by SSDA-style methods.
- The change is targeted and low-risk while having high potential impact on accuracy.

### Description
- Added `proto_src`, `proto_tgt_l`, and `proto_tgt_u` `DataLoader`s in `build_dataloaders()` that use `shuffle=False` and `drop_last=False` and included them in the returned `loaders` dict.
- In `main()` extracted these `proto_*` loaders from `loaders` and wired them into prototype building calls by passing `loader_tgt_l=proto_tgt_l_loader` and `loader_tgt_u=proto_tgt_u_loader` to `build_proto_bank()`.
- Switched `compute_class_weights()` to use the stable loaders by passing `loader_src=proto_src_loader` (when `args.class_weight_use_src`), `loader_tgt_l=proto_tgt_l_loader`, and `loader_tgt_u=proto_tgt_u_loader`.
- No other training logic or training-data loaders were altered; training sampling behavior remains unchanged for the optimization loop.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.
- Manual runtime/behavioral validation was not performed as part of this PR.

💡 What: Added request body logging to the Cerebras API client when errors occur.
🎯 Why: Previously, API errors (like 400 Bad Request) were logged with only the status code and response body, making it impossible to know *what* invalid data was sent (especially for complex prompts).
📊 Impact: Debugging API failures is now significantly easier as logs show "Status + Response + Request Context".
🔬 Example: `Warning: Model qwen-3-32b failed (status 400): {"error":"invalid_request"} | Req: {"model":"qwen-3-32b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}]...`

Bootstrap a practice repository for writing unit tests against legacy Node.js dependencies, featuring three service classes with comprehensive test coverage using specified library versions.

## Services Implemented

- **MongoDB Service** (`mongodb@3.6.12`): CRUD operations, pagination, filtering
- **External API Service** (`axios@^1.8.4`): HTTP client with auth, timeout handling, error normalization
- **AWS S3 Service** (`@aws-sdk/client-s3@3.758.0`): File operations including multipart uploads, streaming downloads, metadata queries

## Test Infrastructure

- 61 tests with 100% coverage using Mocha + Chai + Sinon + Nock
- Each service tested for success paths, error conditions, and edge cases (null handling, disconnection, 404s)
- Async operations properly stubbed at driver/client level

## Example Usage

```javascript
const MongoDBService = require('./src/services/mongodb.service');
const mongoService = new MongoDBService('mongodb://localhost:27017');

await mongoService.connect('mydb');
const user = await mongoService.createUser({ name: 'John', email: 'john@example.com' });
await mongoService.updateUser(user.id, { name: 'Jane' });
```

body:
The webhook handler was processing 66,000+ API invocations per month due to triggering on every pool update during active battles and lacking table filtering. Quick Battles leaderboard required correct `is_quick_battle` flags based on Audius music links.

## Changes

### Webhook Handler (`api/webhooks/battles.ts`)
- **Table filtering**: Skip events from non-battles tables
- **Enhanced logging**: Winner status (Artist A/B/TBD), pool values, skip reasons

```typescript
// Skip non-battles tables
if (payload.table !== 'battles') {
  console.log(`⏭️ Skipping webhook trigger for unrelated table: ${payload.table}`);
  return Response.json({ success: true, action: 'skipped_table' });
}

// Active battle updates already skipped when winner_decided = false
if (!battleData.winner_decided) {
  console.log(`⏭️ Skipping UPDATE for active battle ${battleId}`);
  return { success: true, action: 'skipped_active_battle' };
}
```

**Expected impact**: 90%+ reduction in webhook invocations (only INSERT and final UPDATE processed)

### Database Migration (`migrations/002_update_quick_battle_flags.sql`)
Updates `is_quick_battle` flag for existing battles using:
- **Primary indicator**: Audius music links (`artist1_music_link LIKE '%audius.co%'`)
- **Secondary**: Duration ≤1200s, naming patterns ("Wavez x", "x Hurric4n3Ike")
- **Safety**: Preserves existing flags, excludes test battles

### Documentation
- `WEBHOOK_IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md`: Deployment instructions, monitoring setup, troubleshooting
- `WEBHOOK_BEHAVIOR_SUMMARY.md`: Implementation overview and expected outcomes

### Quick Battles Leaderboard
Verified existing implementation:
- Fallback mechanism (view → battles table) working correctly
- Song aggregation by Audius track functional
- Column mapping with comprehensive fallback chain

## Deployment

1. Code deploys automatically to Vercel on merge
2. Apply database migration manually (see `WEBHOOK_IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md`)
3. Monitor webhook logs for "skipped_table" and "skipped_active_battle" events

> ### Steps to Fix the Webhook Behavior and Quick Battles Leaderboard
> 
> Based on the code investigation, here are the detailed steps to address the identified issues:
> 
> ---
> 
> ### **1. Fix Webhook Logic**
> The webhook triggers repeatedly due to unreliable status handling. Adjust the webhook logic to rely on blockchain data directly for battle finality:
> 
> #### Implementation
> - **File**: `api/webhooks/battles.ts`
> - **Existing Issue**: The webhook logic does not stop when `status` remains unchanged (e.g., `ACTIVE` or `COMPLETED`).
> - **Fix Summary**: Allow the webhook to finalize battles based purely on blockchain data rather than waiting for status changes.
> 
> #### Code Change
> 1. Skip UPDATE calls unless the `winner_decided` flag is true.
> 2. Use blockchain data to detect the correct `winner_artist_a`.
> 
> ```typescript
> async function handleBattleUpdate(payload) {
>   if (!payload.winner_decided) {
>     console.log("Skipping webhook update; battle winner not decided yet.");
>     return;

>

>   console.log("Updating battle; winner confirmed.");
>   await updateBattleDatabase(payload.battle_id, {

>   });
> }
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ### **2. Optimize Quick Battles Leaderboard**
> #### Root Causes
> - **Database Table Mapping Issue**: The `is_quick_battle` flag is not reliable in identifying quick battles.
> - **API Failure for Leaderboard**: Missing fallback to the table directly when the view fails causes zero entries.
> 
> #### Fix Steps
> 1. **Update the Database Query Logic**:
>    - **File**: `services/supabaseClient.ts`
>    - Add fallback to `battles` table when `v_quick_battle_leaderboard_public` fails:
>    
> ```typescript
> export async function fetchQuickBattleLeaderboardFromDB(): Promise<QuickBattleLeaderboardEntry[] | null> {
>   // Fallback to battles table when view fails
>   const fallbackQuery = await supabase
>     .from('battles')
>     .select(`
>       artist1_name,
>       artist2_name,
>       winner_artist_a,
>       trade_count,
>       unique_traders,
>       created_at
>     `)
>     .eq('is_quick_battle', true)
>     .limit(200);
> 
>   // Aggregate data from battles table
>   const aggregatedData = aggregateQuickBattlesBySong(fallbackQuery.data);
>   return aggregatedData;
> }
> ```

> 2. **Ensure Correct Flag Usage in Database Schema**:
>    - Modify the `battles` table to correctly set `is_quick_battle` during inserts.
>    - **Required Migration**:

> UPDATE battles

> ---

body: Closes #10 (Heatmap des tirs adverse) Closes #5 (PvP) J'ai totalement refait le systeme de heatmap - Ajout d'un historique de tir pour J1 et J2 - Ajout de la heatmap des tirs adverses J'ai ajouté trois mode de pondération des tirs sur la heatmap, à savoir: - Aucune pondération: chaque tir à une valeur de 1 - Pondération privilégiant les tirs les plus récents. Les tirs les plus récent ont une valeur tendant vers 0, les tirs les plus anciens ont une valeur tendant vers 1. Donc valeur des tirs récent < valeur des tirs ancien. Cela permet d'évaluer la stratégie de début de partie de l'adversaire. author: dharshan-kumarj
body:
This pull request introduces major improvements to the Nexus Vault application's environment configuration, Docker setup, and background processing via RabbitMQ and email notifications. The changes enable a more secure, production-ready, and easily configurable deployment using Docker Compose, environment variables, and a dedicated worker service for asynchronous tasks like sending emails. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

**Environment & Configuration Management:**

* Added a comprehensive `.env.example` file for environment variable configuration, covering MongoDB, RabbitMQ, SMTP, and app settings. This allows for secure and flexible management of sensitive credentials and deployment parameters.
* Updated `docker-compose.yml` to load environment variables from the `.env` file for all services, replacing hardcoded values and improving portability and security.
* Added a `QUICKSTART.md` guide for fast setup, including prerequisites, step-by-step instructions, troubleshooting, and file structure overview.

**Docker & Service Architecture:**

* Refactored Docker setup to include a dedicated `worker` service (with its own `Dockerfile.worker`) for processing queued tasks, and improved SSL/TLS support in both web and worker containers for secure MongoDB connections. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6c773088e9ae1f54cc74d1f78c5d15a8b152f53a0866e29ed4b82f4906c25642R1-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b8f3af14144ec1fec5c0b20e6ae22513d16c5dab3681128769c8b0e5c9b33900L3-R13) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-82d455a1fee9ebdc8092e2ff1ee4421c7e9871892c60ca0b43c4cc7ebaeb3ea2L12-R44)
* Integrated RabbitMQ as a managed service with persistent storage and web dashboard, facilitating reliable background task processing.

**MongoDB & RabbitMQ Integration:**

* Enhanced MongoDB connection logic in `Database.php` to support robust TLS/SSL handling, dynamic CA certificate detection, and optional allowance for invalid certificates for debugging.
* Improved `QueueManager.php` to use environment-based RabbitMQ credentials, set connection timeouts, ensure durable queue declaration, and provide better error logging and handling for queue operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b7852bb39710492a01788d5a2bc9bd617d84c2a2cdcc7f233f6f9b2184a89502L2-R2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b7852bb39710492a01788d5a2bc9bd617d84c2a2cdcc7f233f6f9b2184a89502L14-R39) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b7852bb39710492a01788d5a2bc9bd617d84c2a2cdcc7f233f6f9b2184a89502L37-R59) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b7852bb39710492a01788d5a2bc9bd617d84c2a2cdcc7f233f6f9b2184a89502R75-R81)

**Background Worker & Email Notifications:**

* Added a new `worker.php` script that listens to RabbitMQ queues and processes tasks such as sending welcome emails via PHPMailer using SMTP credentials from the environment. Includes retry logic, queue acknowledgment, and logging.
* Updated `composer.json` to include `phpmailer/phpmailer` for email functionality.

These changes collectively modernize the application's deployment, configuration, and background processing, making it more scalable, secure, and maintainable.

body:
💡 **What:** Optimized `AdBlocker.isAdHostRaw` by converting the keyword list to an array and using an explicit loop. Also removed a duplicate constant in `MovieRepository`.

🎯 **Why:** The AdBlocker runs on every network request. Iterating a `List` creates an `Iterator` object each time. Using an `Array` with an index-based loop (or explicit for-each which compiles to index loop on arrays) eliminates this allocation, reducing GC pressure in a hot path.

📊 **Impact:**
*   Eliminates 1 object allocation per network request check.
*   ~40% faster iteration speed (Micro-benchmark: 6253ms vs 10676ms for 10M iterations).

🔬 **Measurement:**
*   Verified logic with `Benchmark.java`.
*   Verified compilation and logic preservation via code review.

author: griffinxd
body:
## 📧 Automated 24-Hour Appointment Reminder System

This PR implements an automated email reminder system that sends reminder emails to patients 24 hours before their scheduled appointments.

### ✨ Features Implemented

- **Automated Cron Job**: Runs every hour to check for upcoming appointments
- **24-Hour Window**: Sends reminders to appointments scheduled 23-24 hours in advance
- **Turkish Localization**: Emails formatted with `tr-TR` locale and `Europe/Istanbul` timezone
- **Error Handling**: Individual error handling per appointment - one failure doesn't stop the entire job
- **Status Tracking**: `reminderSent` flag prevents duplicate emails

### 🔧 Changes Made

#### Database Schema
- Added `reminderSent` Boolean field (default: false) to Appointment model
- Installed `node-cron` package for job scheduling

#### Core Implementation
- **`src/jobs/reminderJob.js`**: Cron job service with appointment query and processing logic
- **`src/services/email.service.js`**: New `sendAppointmentReminderEmail()` function with beautiful HTML template
- **`src/server.js`**: Integrated cron job initialization on server startup

#### Test Scripts
- **`scripts/createTestAppointments.js`**: Create test appointments with any email(s)
- **`scripts/testReminderJob.js`**: Manually trigger reminder emails for testing

### 🧪 How to Test

1. Create test appointments:
   node scripts/createTestAppointments.js your-email@example.com
   2. Trigger reminder emails (bypasses 24-hour window):
   node scripts/testReminderJob.js your-email@example.com
   ### 📝 Technical Details

- Cron schedule: `0 * * * *` (runs every hour at minute 0)
- Date format: DD.MM.YYYY (parsed from Appointment model)
- Time format: HH:MM (displayed in Istanbul timezone)
- Status filter: Only sends to APPROVED appointments
- Comprehensive logging for monitoring and debugging

### ✅ Commits

- `d503a38` - Add reminderSent field to Appointment model
- `4d98a40` - Create appointment reminder job service
- `89ee1e1` - Implement hourly cron job for appointment reminders
- `5739b30` - Integrate appointment reminder cron job into server

author: mrzoller
body: ## Summary This PR addresses three critical security/reliability issues and includes several non-critical improvements. 1. **Auth URL injection / broken mirror URLs**: `get_authenticated_url()` was vulnerable to URL corruption or host injection due to direct string interpolation of token name/value. This is fixed by normalizing instance URLs, validating schemes, and percent-encoding userinfo when composing Git URLs. 2. **Header injection via export filename**: Export download filenames derived from database data could allow CR/LF injection into `Content-Disposition` headers. This is fixed by sanitizing the filename to a conservative set of characters. 3. **Hardened encryption key handling**: * Encryption key initialization is now lazy to prevent filesystem writes at import time in restricted environments. * Added support for `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (direct key via env var) and `ENCRYPTION_KEY_PATH` (custom path via env var). * Improved key reading (`strip()`), added best-effort `chmod 600`, and clearer decryption failure messages. ## Test plan - [x] `pytest` (All 26 tests pass) - [x] Manual verification (Auth URL construction, export filename sanitization, encryption key loading/decryption) ## Notes * **Breaking changes**: None, existing functionality should be preserved. * **Follow-ups**: None immediately required. * **Pydantic v2**: Updated `Config.from_attributes` to `model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)` to remove deprecation warnings. * **Starlette**: Fixed `TemplateResponse` call signature. ---

body:
…readsheet storage.

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: User-controlled input (e.g., case names, evidence content, tags) was written directly to XLSX cells without sanitization. Strings starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` could be interpreted as malicious formulas by Excel. 🎯 Impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) or data exfiltration if a malicious spreadsheet is opened in Excel. 🔧 Fix:
- Created `SpreadsheetUtils.sanitizeForSpreadsheet` to prepend `'` to risky strings.
- Updated `LocalFileStorageService` to sanitize all user inputs before writing.
- Specifically handled `Tags` list sanitization. ✅ Verification: Added `FormulaInjectionTest.kt` to verify sanitization logic for various attack vectors and edge cases.

## Summary by Sourcery

Sanitize all user-controlled strings before writing them into XLSX spreadsheets to eliminate formula/CSV injection vectors.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent Excel formula injection by escaping strings that begin with spreadsheet formula metacharacters before storing them in exhibits, cases, evidence, allegations, and transcript-related cells.

Enhancements:
- Introduce a reusable SpreadsheetUtils.sanitizeForSpreadsheet helper for safe spreadsheet output and apply it across LocalFileStorageService.
- Add regression tests to validate spreadsheet sanitization behavior for dangerous inputs and tag handling.
- Record the incident and remediation steps in an internal Sentinel security note.

>

> - **ALWAYS** include debug console logging for significant operations
> - Use the existing debug helper functions:

>   - `debugWarn(message, ... args)` - For warning conditions

## Summary
- Added GetTenantProvisioningStatus RPC to tenant service for querying overall tenant status and per-service provisioning details
- Implemented repository layer with FindProvisioningStatusByTenantID method to query tenant_provisioning_status table
- Created gRPC handler with proper error handling, status enum conversion, and comprehensive unit tests

## Task Master Reference
- **Tag**: 8-multi-tenancy
- **Task ID**: 72

## Changes Made
- **Proto definition**: Added GetTenantProvisioningStatus RPC with ServiceProvisioningStatus message, request/response types, and HTTP gateway annotation for GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/provisioning-status. Restored deprecated provisioning_hint field for backward compatibility.
- **Repository methods**: Implemented FindProvisioningStatusByTenantID with ProvisioningStatus domain struct, proper null handling for optional fields (started_at, completed_at, error_message), and comprehensive unit tests.
- **gRPC handler**: Created GetTenantProvisioningStatus method that queries tenant table for overall status and tenant_provisioning_status for per-service details. Includes NotFound error handling, status enum conversion, structured logging, and unit tests.

## Test Plan
- **Unit tests**: Mock repository queries, verify response structure with multiple services, test NotFound scenarios, validate status enum conversions
- **Integration tests**: Create tenant, insert mock provisioning_status records, call GetTenantProvisioningStatus endpoint, verify per-service details returned correctly, test error handling for non-existent tenants

  - Added to docs site navigation in `site/docs/index.html` under "Implementation Docs" section

## Example Test Pattern

Using fake client for v2 controller tests (based on existing patterns):

```go
func TestArgoCDProviderReconciler_BasicReconciliation(t *testing.T) {
    fakeClient := fake.NewClientBuilder().

}
```

body:
## Summary

Replace the hidden ellipsis dropdown menu on agenda kanban cards with inline action buttons that appear on hover/focus for faster, more intuitive interactions.

## What Changed

- **Status buttons** (Pending, In Progress, Completed) now appear inline on hover
- **Edit and Delete** buttons appear alongside status buttons
- **Current status** is visually highlighted with a background color
- **Delete button** has red destructive hover state
- **Accessibility**: `aria-label` on all buttons, `role="group"` for action container, keyboard focus support via `group-focus-within`
- **Smooth transition**: 150ms fade-in for action reveal
- **Removed**: Ellipsis menu, dropdown, and related state management (cleaner code)

## Design Decisions

1. **Hover action bar pattern** - Follows modern kanban UX (Trello, Linear, Asana)
2. **Icon-only with tooltips** - Compact but accessible with `title` attributes
3. **Visual divider** - Separates status buttons from edit/delete for clarity
4. **Focus support** - Actions appear on keyboard focus, not just mouse hover

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Status buttons appear on card hover/focus
- [x] Edit and Delete buttons appear on hover/focus
- [x] Current status is highlighted
- [x] Proper `aria-label` attributes for accessibility
- [x] Tooltips show action name on hover
- [x] Actions appear on keyboard focus (not just mouse hover)
- [x] Smooth 150ms fade transition
- [x] Delete button has red destructive styling on hover
- [x] Ellipsis menu removed entirely

### Motivation

author: jpturcotte
body:
### Motivation
- Logging previously called `.item()` (and thus synced) per-parameter which caused many GPU synchronizations during training and eval diagnostics. 
- The goal is to batch parameter and gradient tensors so norms are computed in a single tensor op and produce only one GPU sync per diagnostic. 
- Inline comments requested guards for empty tensors to avoid `torch.cat` on empty lists. 

### Description
- Replaced per-parameter `.item()` accumulation in training and evaluation logging in `train.py` with batched concatenation using `params = [param.detach().view(-1) for param in model.parameters() if param.numel() > 0]` and `all_params = torch.cat(params)` followed by `all_params.norm(2.0, dtype=torch.float32).item()`, and return `float('nan')` for empty models. 
- Rewrote `module_grad_weight_norm` in `utils.py` to collect non-empty weight tensors and gradient tensors, compute `weight_norm` and `grad_norm` via `torch.cat(...).norm(2.0, dtype=torch.float32).item()` inside `torch.no_grad()`, and fall back to `weight_norm = float('nan')` or `grad_norm = 0.0` as appropriate. 
- Added guards that filter out tensors with `param.numel() == 0` before concatenation to prevent errors on empty tensors. 
- Preserved the existing NaN detection and logging behavior while switching to batched operations to minimize GPU synchronizations. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change. 
- The change consists of local code edits to `train.py` and `utils.py` and was committed without running the test suite. 
- Runtime profiling or validation of reduced GPU syncs was not performed as part of automated steps. 
- There are no reported test failures because tests were not invoked.

author: scratch-ml
body:
Do not assume each beam returns a fixed number of logprob entries. Track the parent beam index per candidate to avoid wrong indexing and potential out-of-bounds when selecting top-k candidates.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose

Fix a regression introduced by PR #19347 (commit `56f45edda`), where the beam search optimization incorrectly assumes `engine_client.generate()` always returns exactly `logprobs_num` candidates per beam. In practice the returned `logprobs` dict may have a variable size (e.g. `logprobs_num + 1`), which can cause wrong parent-beam mapping (`idx // logprobs_num`), leading to incorrect results or potential out-of-bounds / mis-indexing.

This PR makes the mapping robust by tracking the parent beam index per candidate token, while keeping the numpy `argpartition` optimization.

FIX #31081

author: toziegler
body:
This PR reduces noise in our binary search benchmark to make potential performance regressions easier to detect.

The benchmark now focuses only on scenarios that matter. Previously, it covered many additional cases, some of which are not relevant in our code, which introduced unnecessary noise.
To further stabilize the results, the benchmark now collects multiple samples, discards the two fastest runs, and reports the third-best result. While this may seem unintuitive, it follows a best practice to mitigate system noise and transient effects as most benchmark distributions are log-normal ( [see](https://lemire.me/blog/2018/01/16/microbenchmarking-calls-for-idealized-conditions/) and  [here](https://github.com/travisdowns/uarch-bench)).

The benchmark also uses a fixed random seed for each benchmark run, improving reproducibility. (The smoke benchmark still uses a random seed.) Finally, an 8 MB allocation was moved from the stack to the heap.

P.S. I want to create a few more benchmarks with @matklad's nice benchmark harness in the next few days.

### Motivation
- Prevent Pro entitlement from bleeding across Firebase accounts on the same device by tying subscriptions to Firebase UIDs.
- Ensure only the Firebase user bound to the StoreKit original transaction receives Pro, and show an error if a subscription is linked to another account.
- Improve observability around subscription binding and entitlement updates for easier debugging.

### Description
- Added binding logic that uses the StoreKit `originalTransactionId` and a `subscriptionBindings/{originalTransactionId}` Firestore document to record and validate the UID-to-subscription binding inside a transaction.
- On purchase/restore/refresh, run a Firestore transaction to create or validate the binding and throw a `linkedToAnotherAccount` error when the binding UID differs from the current `Auth` UID, and update the `users/{uid}/entitlements/pro` document only when binding succeeds.
- Fixed Firestore async usage by awaiting `setData` for user entitlement updates and preserved the transactional `runTransaction` flow with proper error handling and continuations.
- Added debug logs for subscription refreshes, binding reads/creates, entitlement updates, binding transaction failures, and entitlement listener errors, and ensured the existing auth-state clearing/listener swap logic remains intact.

body:
### Motivation

- Replace the legacy time-based 3-phase rule-selection with an episode-level meta-learning baseline so rules get commitment and clearer credit assignment. 
- Provide a standardized, pluggable rule API so heuristics (FOQ/POQ/SM/EOQ) can be compared fairly. 
- Offer a minimal, debuggable serial supply-chain env and a meta wrapper that executes a chosen rule for a whole episode. 
- Stabilize learning (avoid NaNs) and modernize runtime dependencies for Colab/NumPy 2.x compatibility.

### Description

- Added standardized rule implementations in `rules/inventory_rules.py` (`BaseRule`, `FOQRule`, `POQRule`, `SilverMealRule`, `EOQRule`) with `get_action(current_inventory, demand_history)` API. 
- Added a minimal physical environment `envs/serial_env.py` and a meta wrapper `envs/meta_wrapper.py` where `reset()` returns a meta-state and `step(rule_idx)` executes the full episode with the selected rule and returns episode-level meta-state and return. 
- Implemented a batched REINFORCE agent in `algorithms/reinforce.py` returning logits (temperature applied in logit space), with batched `record()`/`update()` flow, reward normalization, entropy bonus and gradient clipping to improve stability. 
- Added a CLI training entry `main_serial.py` (flags: `--num-episodes`, `--batch-size`, `--temp-start`, `--eval-interval`, etc.), integrated a meta-learning branch in `train_env.py` (via `get_env_class()`), made `gymnasium` the preferred import with `gym` fallback, and updated `requirements.txt` to modern versions (including `gymnasium`).

## Summary - Fix rendering issues when range items have different conditional branches (e.g., different input types in a form) - Add StaticsMap to RangeData for hash-based deduplication of per-item statics - Each item with different statics gets a `_sk` (statics key) referencing its statics in StaticsMap ## Problem When range items produce different statics due to conditionals (like `{{if eq .Type "number"}}...{{else}}...{{end}}`), only the first item's statics were used for all items. This caused: - Wrong input types being rendered (text input statics used for number input) - Browser warnings like "The specified value 'World' cannot be parsed" ## Solution - Collect statics from each range item during tree building - Hash statics arrays to detect unique variants - For homogeneous ranges (all same statics): use existing single `s` format - For heterogeneous ranges: use new `sm` (statics map) with per-item `_sk` keys ## Wire Format Homogeneous (unchanged): ```json {"d": [...items...], "s": ["

author: fasterthanlime
body:
… #1350)

This commit fixes the inability to parse nested TOML table headers like `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]` when the intermediate keys map to struct values in a HashMap.

**Root Cause:**

The table header parser had an overly restrictive check in `begin_field_or_list_item()` that rejected ANY HashMap value with `Def::Undefined`, treating it as "scalar-like" and incompatible with table headers. However, structs often have `Def::Undefined` even though they CAN serve as tables (they have fields that can receive key-value pairs).

**The Fix:**

1. Changed the scalar-like check to ONLY reject `Def::Scalar` types
2. Added a guard so the check only applies when `is_last_in_path=true` (when the value will directly receive key-value pairs)
3. For middle path elements (`is_last_in_path=false`), we skip the check entirely since we'll navigate deeper into the structure

This allows table headers like:
- `[target.x86_64.dependencies]` where target: HashMap<String, TargetSpec>
- `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]` (the real-world Cargo.toml case)

The fix is minimal and conservative - we only reject definite scalars, and allow `Def::Undefined` types to proceed. If they're truly incompatible, the subsequent field navigation will fail with a clear error.

**Testing:**

Added comprehensive tests covering both 2-level and 3-level nested table headers, with and without key-value pairs, and with quoted keys. All 195 existing facet-toml tests still pass.

author: umarhayat-dev
body:
✦ Cell Broadcast Alert Normalization
What was added

A dedicated normalization pipeline for Cell Broadcast alerts

Clear separation between:

raw incoming data (vendor / platform dependent)

internal Alert model (app-wide contract)

Key details

Introduced a RawCellBroadcastMessage type to represent untrusted / variable input payloads

Implemented normalizeCellBroadcast() as a pure function that converts raw messages into the unified Alert type

Explicitly sets:

source → CELL

verified → true (cell broadcast is considered a trusted government channel)

expiresAt → derived from timestamp with a fixed validity window

Severity values (string or numeric) are mapped deterministically to HazardLevel

Location data is safely defaulted when missing, allowing area-wide broadcasts to be represented without breaking downstream consumers

Why this matters

Keeps platform-specific chaos at the edge

Prevents UI and store layers from dealing with inconsistent payloads

Makes future Android native listeners trivial:
listen → normalize → store

✦ Hazard Level Semantic System
What was added

A centralized utility layer defining what hazard levels mean, not how they are displayed

Key details

Introduced HazardMetadata describing:

human-readable label

description

severity priority

semantic color (not UI-specific)

Implemented utilities:

getHazardMetadata(level) for consistent representation

compareHazard(a, b) for sorting and escalation

isSevereOrAbove(level) for decision-making logic

Explicit ordering enforced:

CRITICAL > SEVERE > MODERATE > LOW

Why this matters

Prevents multiple features from redefining “severe” differently

Ensures consistent sorting, escalation, and filtering across the app

Keeps UI layers dumb and declarative (no hardcoded severity rules)

✦ Architectural Guarantees

This PR does not:

Add UI components or styling

Add native Android code or listeners

Modify global store structure

Introduce side effects or background tasks

This PR does:

Establish stable contracts for alert ingestion

Centralize disaster severity semantics

Enable safe parallel development of:

Bluetooth mesh alerts

Location-based alerts

Satellite alerts (future)

✦ How this will be used next

Native Android cell broadcast listeners will call normalizeCellBroadcast()

Normalized alerts will be added to the global alert store

UI and notification systems will consume hazard metadata without custom logic

✦ Testing & Safety

All logic is deterministic and pure

TypeScript compilation verified

No behavioral changes to existing app flow

Summary

This PR builds core infrastructure, not features.
It intentionally prioritizes correctness, consistency, and future scalability over immediacy.

## Summary

Successfully implemented an interactive object recognition learning system for Raspberry Pi 4B and Zero 2W with camera, MobileNetV2 deep learning features via TFLite, audio output, voice input, and **web browser interface** capabilities.

### ✅ Recent Fix

**TFLite Quantized Model Support** - Fixed tensor type mismatch error when using quantized MobileNetV2 models. The system now automatically detects whether the TFLite model expects uint8 (quantized) or float32 input and handles preprocessing accordingly.

### 📦 All Features Implemented

- [x] Create project structure and dependencies (requirements.txt)
- [x] Implement camera capture module for RPi Camera
- [x] Implement image feature extraction using pre-trained model
- [x] Implement online learning classifier (incremental learning)

- [x] Make TensorFlow Lite optional with graceful fallback
- [x] Install TensorFlow Lite from system packages
- [x] Add LiteRT (ai-edge-litert) support for Python 3.13+/Debian Trixie
- [x] Add MobileNetV2 TFLite model with automatic download and integration
- [x] Fix TFLite model download with validation and multiple mirrors
- [x] Add web interface mode with Flask-based UI
- [x] **Fix quantized TFLite model tensor type handling (NEW)** ✨
- [x] Create main application loop with camera and learning logic
- [x] Add README with installation and usage instructions
- [x] Test the application flow (all tests passing)
- [x] Add automated test suite
- [x] Run code review and address all feedback
- [x] Run security checks (0 vulnerabilities)
- [x] Add example interaction documentation
- [x] Add automated setup script

### 🔧 TFLite Quantized Model Fix

**Problem:** 
`ValueError: Cannot set tensor: Got value of type FLOAT32` occurred when using quantized MobileNetV2 models downloaded from Google Coral or TensorFlow Hub. Quantized models expect uint8 input [0-255] but the code was providing float32 input [-1, 1].

**Solution (commit in progress):**

Enhanced `feature_extractor.py` to automatically detect and handle both quantized and float models:

1. **Input type detection:**
   - Checks `input_details[0]['dtype']` to determine expected input type
   - For uint8 models: keeps image in [0, 255] range as uint8
   - For float32 models: normalizes to [-1, 1] range as before

2. **Output dequantization:**
   - Checks `output_details[0]['dtype']` for quantized outputs
   - Automatically dequantizes uint8 outputs using scale and zero_point
   - Ensures consistent float32 feature vectors for classifier

**Technical details:**
```python
# Auto-detect input type
input_dtype = self.input_details[0]['dtype']

if input_dtype == np.uint8:
    # Quantized model: expects uint8 input [0, 255]
    img_array = np.expand_dims(resized, axis=0).astype(np.uint8)
else:
    # Float model: scale to [-1, 1]
    img_array = np.expand_dims(resized, axis=0).astype(np.float32)
    img_array = (img_array / 127.5) - 1.0

# Auto-dequantize output if needed
output_dtype = self.output_details[0]['dtype']
if output_dtype == np.uint8:
    scale, zero_point = self.output_details[0]['quantization']
    features = scale * (features.astype(np.float32) - zero_point)
```

**Benefits:**
- ✅ Works with both quantized (uint8) and float (float32) TFLite models
- ✅ Automatic detection - no configuration needed
- ✅ Proper dequantization for accurate feature extraction
- ✅ Compatible with Google Coral, TensorFlow Hub, and official TensorFlow models
- ✅ Maintains performance benefits of quantized models

### 🌐 Web Interface Mode

**Full-stack web application for browser-based interaction:**

**Key features:**
- 📱 **Browser-based UI** - Access from any device on the network
- 🖼️ **Live camera feed** - See captured images in real-time
- 🎯 **Visual predictions** - Display predictions with confidence scores
- 🖱️ **Click-to-learn** - Point-and-click interface for teaching objects
- 📊 **Live statistics** - Real-time dashboard of known objects
- 🎨 **Modern design** - Responsive, gradient UI that works on desktop and mobile
- 🔕 **No audio/voice** - Replaces audio I/O with visual web forms
- 🌐 **Network accessible** - Access from any device on local network
- ⚡ **RESTful API** - JSON endpoints for capture, learn, and status

**Usage:**
```bash
# Start web server (accessible from all network interfaces)
python3 main.py --web

# Custom host and port
python3 main.py --web --host 192.168.1.100 --port 8080

# Then access from browser:
# http://<raspberry-pi-ip>:5000
```

### 🔧 Feature Extraction Modes

The system supports three feature extraction modes with automatic fallback:

**1. TFLite + MobileNetV2 (Best - Recommended) ✨**
- Uses `ai-edge-litert` (LiteRT) or `tflite_runtime` interpreter
- MobileNetV2 model in TFLite format (~3.4 MB)
- Supports both quantized (uint8) and float (float32) models ✨ NEW

- Low memory usage - works great on Zero 2W

**2. Full TensorFlow (Heavier)**

- More memory intensive
- Mainly for development/testing

**3. Simple Features (Lightweight Fallback)**

- Always works as final fallback
- Sufficient for basic object recognition

author: tombonator3000
body:
Root cause: In ParticleSystem constructor, pre-allocated particles started with active=true (from reset() call in Particle constructor), but _activeCount was initialized to 0. When getParticle() searched for inactive particles, it found none and fell through to reuse existing particles without incrementing _activeCount. This caused draw() to early-exit since _activeCount === 0.

Fix: Set particle.active = false after creating each particle in the pool, so getParticle() can properly find and activate them.
