author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Fixed issues with achievement notification system and improved code quality. Implemented a signal-based architecture for completion achievement notifications.

## Changes Made

### simple_ui.gd
- [x] Added deduplication logic to prevent showing multiple copies of the same achievement progress
- [x] Only the latest state of an achievement is kept in the queue
- [x] **Completion achievements are always displayed last in the queue**
- [x] Regular achievements are inserted before any completion achievement in the queue
- [x] Fixed all trailing whitespace lint errors

### chief_mint_source.gd (base class)
- [x] Added `completion_achievement_unlocked` signal to base class
- [x] Establishes contract for sources to notify when completion achievements are auto-completed

### chief_mint_source_file.gd
- [x] Added type hints for completion_mint (ChiefMintResource) and non_completion_mints (Array[ChiefMintResource])
- [x] Simplified to handle single completion mint instead of array
- [x] Emits `completion_achievement_unlocked` signal when completion achievement is triggered
- [x] Only emits signal if completion mint was previously incomplete (prevents duplicates)

### chief_mint_singleton.gd
- [x] Connected to `completion_achievement_unlocked` signal from source
- [x] Simplified increment_progress() by removing manual completion checking
- [x] Added signal handler to forward completion notifications as progress_changed
- [x] Fixed all trailing whitespace and line length lint errors
- [x] Improved code readability and maintainability

## How It Works

1. **Deduplication**: When a new notification for an achievement arrives, any existing notification for that achievement is removed from the queue before adding the new one
2. **Completion Achievement via Signal**: The source emits `completion_achievement_unlocked` signal when it auto-completes the completion achievement. The singleton listens to this signal and emits `progress_changed` to notify the UI
3. **Completion Always Last**: When adding achievements to the queue:
   - Completion achievements are always appended to the end
   - Regular achievements are inserted before any completion achievement
   - This ensures completion achievements are always displayed last
4. **Clean Architecture**: The singleton no longer needs to manually check completion state - the source notifies it directly through a signal when completion happens
5. **Single Completion Mint**: Simplified all logic to handle only a single completion achievement instead of treating it as a list
6. **All lint checks pass**: No trailing whitespace, proper line lengths, clean code with proper type hints

## Testing

The demo scene test button can be used to verify:
- Multiple rapid triggers of the same achievement only show the final state
- Completion achievement appears when all other achievements are complete
- **Completion achievement is always displayed last, even if triggered before other achievements finish displaying**
- No duplicate notifications are shown

These workflows previously used direct `push` triggers, which meant they couldn't be called by thin wrapper workflows in individual package repos. This change aligns them with the existing pattern used by `r-cmd-check.yaml`, `lint.yaml`, `pkgdown.yaml`, etc.

## Test plan
- [ ] Thin wrappers in templ.rpkg can call these workflows
- [ ] Workflows execute correctly when triggered via wrapper

author: houngansi
body:
…equiredDependencies

The VisualizationService was failing to initialize because GetRequiredDependencies() declared dependencies on services that are not registered in ServiceLocator:
- Service.ActorFactory
- Service.AttachmentSystem
- Service.VisualController

These services are actually OPTIONAL - the code uses TryGetService() and handles their absence gracefully. By returning an empty container (like AbilityService does), the service can now initialize successfully.

The DataService dependency is already handled via InitParams.RequiredServices in SystemCoordinator.RegisterCoreServices().

Root cause: ServiceLocator::InitializeService fails when any declared dependency is not found in the registry, even if the service handles absence gracefully.

author: scrimshawlife-ctrl
body:
### Motivation

- Add the PR1 "doctrine spine" to encode ritual phases and compressed intent semantics so intent enters the system as a typed symbol, not arbitrary dicts.
- Provide a deterministic, canonical compilation step from intent to a single structured parameter object (`ParamBundle`) to reduce sprawl and prepare for ritual enforcement in later PRs.
- Preserve existing generation behavior via a compat-mode adapter so legacy pipelines continue to work.

### Description

- Added a new module `beatoven/core/doctrine.py` containing:
  - `IntentToken`, `RitualPhase`, `RitualPlan`, and `ParamBundle` dataclasses/types.
  - `Compiler` protocol and a concrete `IntentCompiler` with a deterministic `compile(...)` implementation and `DEFAULTS` mapping.
  - Deterministic seed helpers: `derive_seed_string` and `derive_seed_int`, and a `to_legacy_params` adapter.
- Wired the compiler into the API (`beatoven/api/main.py`):
  - Registered `app.state.intent_compiler = IntentCompiler()`.
  - The `/generate` flow now constructs an `IntentToken`, derives a deterministic seed, compiles to a `ParamBundle`, and uses bundle fields (tempo, duration, key_root, scale, resonance, density, tension, drift, contrast) while still translating to ABX fields and invoking existing engines.
  - The compiler accepts `memory` overrides (compat mode) so existing request fields can be honored when necessary.
- Added tests in `beatoven/tests/test_doctrine.py`:
  - `test_intent_compiler_determinism` (same `IntentToken` + seed → identical `ParamBundle`).
  - `test_generate_smoke` which hits the API `/generate` endpoint as a smoke test.

### Testing

- Ran the new unit tests and a small API smoke test via `pytest beatoven/tests/test_doctrine.py beatoven/tests/test_api.py`.
- Test run failed during collection with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'` (missing `pyyaml` dependency), so tests did not execute to completion.
- Added deterministic unit test (`test_intent_compiler_determinism`) and a smoke API test; both are present and will run once `pyyaml` (or the repo's test dependencies) are available in the test environment.
- Manual verification: the `/generate` endpoint was updated to use `IntentToken` → `IntentCompiler.compile(...)` → `ParamBundle` internally while keeping the downstream generation calls unchanged.

author: kossencrap
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a lightweight UI to visualize existing aggregated metrics (volume, mentions, co-mentions, sentiment) produced by the metrics exports in `data/processed/metrics/*.parquet`.
- Surface sentiment ratios computed from labeled sentence events and make them available as weekly/monthly exports.
- Allow users to drill down from charts to concrete sentence-level evidence stored in SQLite via existing evidence utilities.
- Offer a simple product filter in the sidebar to focus charts and evidence on a single product or partner.

### Description

- Added a Streamlit dashboard script at `scripts/metrics_dashboard.py` that renders publication volume, product mentions, co-mentions, and sentiment ratio charts and includes evidence drill-down using `fetch_sentence_evidence`.
- Added a sentiment export CLI at `scripts/export_sentiment_metrics.py` which aggregates sentiment ratios via `src.analytics.time_series.sentiment_bucket_counts` and writes weekly/monthly parquet (or JSON fallback) files to `data/processed/metrics`.
- Charts use `pandas`/`altair` when available and fall back to basic plotting/JSON parsing when optional deps are missing, and the dashboard reads metrics files from the configured metrics directory.
- The dashboard sidebar exposes a product selector and optional co-mention partner filter, and each chart contains a button/expander to load sentence evidence from the SQLite DB path configured in the sidebar.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed for these new scripts during this change.
- Manual runtime checks were not performed as part of the commit.
- The dashboard and export scripts guard optional imports (`streamlit`, `pandas`, `altair`) and will print guidance if the dependencies are missing.
- Basic CLI/IO behaviors were exercised by static code inspection and integration with the existing `src.analytics` utilities.

body:
# PR #5: Retro documentation: Add DataSourcesStore, DataSourceRef, Field attributes and expression language

**Author:** Kassko
**Created:** 2025-12-18  
**Merged:** 2025-12-18  

---

Adds centralized DataSource configuration with id-based referencing, field name mapping, batch property hydration, and expression language for dependency chains.

## New Attributes

**DataSourcesStore** - Class-level attribute grouping DataSources with unique ids:
```php
#[DataSourcesStore([
    new DataSource(id: 'personSource', class: PersonDataSource::class, 
                   method: 'getData', args: ['#id'], supplySeveralFields: true),
    new DataSource(id: 'carSource', class: CarRepository::class, 
                   method: 'find', args: ["expr(source('personSource')['car_id'])"])
])]
class Person { /* ... */ }
```

**DataSourceRef** - References DataSource by id instead of repeating configuration:
```php
#[DataSourceRef(id: 'personSource')]
private ?string $name = null;
```

**Field** - Maps property names to different data keys:
```php
#[DataSourceRef(id: 'personSource')]
#[Field(name: 'first_name')]
private ?string $firstName = null;  // Reads from 'first_name' key
```

## Batch Hydration

**supplySeveralFields** option on DataSource:
- `false` (default): Returns value directly, or array with property names as keys for same-signature properties
- `true`: Single call hydrates all properties with matching DataSourceRef in one execution

```php
// Single call to personSource hydrates firstName, name, and email
new DataSource(id: 'personSource', /* ... */, supplySeveralFields: true)
```

## Expression Language

**Property references**: `#id` resolves to `$this->id`

**Source expressions**: `expr(source('personSource')['car_id'])` executes DataSource and extracts array key

**Dependency resolution**: Loading `car` automatically loads `personSource` first, caches result

## Implementation

- `src/Expression/` - ExpressionParser and SourceFunctionProvider for evaluation and caching
- `src/Metadata/AttributeReader` - Extended with methods for new attributes and DataSource map building
- `src/LazyLoader/LazyLoader` - Refactored to handle store resolution, batch hydration, expression evaluation
- Source ids validated with `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+` regex, error messages sanitized

## Testing

12 new integration tests covering DataSourcesStore, Field mapping, expression language, dependency chains, and result caching. All existing tests pass.

author: agent2-workflow[bot]
body:
## Summary

Add Docker-based build scripts to create SSH-enabled MPC 3.6 firmware on Windows:

- **build-mpc-ssh-firmware.ps1**: Main PowerShell build script that orchestrates the Docker container
- **patch-mpc-ssh.sh**: SSH enablement script executed inside Docker
- **README.md**: Complete documentation with usage instructions

## Why This Is Needed

TheKikGen's SSH firmware is only available up to version 3.4.2.13. Installing that would downgrade from MPC 3.6 and lose all the new features (Linear Arranger, Disk Streaming, 8 Layers per Pad, STEM Separation, etc.).

This builder enables SSH on MPC 3.6 while **retaining the new UI**.

## How It Works

1. Uses Docker with `--privileged` to loop-mount the ext4 rootfs
2. Modifies `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`:
   - `PermitRootLogin yes`
   - `PasswordAuthentication yes`
   - `PermitEmptyPasswords yes`
3. Enables `sshd.service` at boot via systemd symlink
4. Repacks using mpcimg2.exe

## Test Plan

- [x] Docker build completes successfully
- [x] Output firmware is 150MB (expected size)
- [ ] Flash to MPC One and verify SSH access
- [ ] Install VNC4MPC bootstrap and test remote control

## Compatible Devices

- MPC Live, MPC X
- MPC One (Gen 1 & 2)
- MPC Live II, MPC One+
- MPC Key 37, MPC Key 61

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

## Problem
When creating worktrees on Windows, the `.kittify/templates/` directory is not copied to the worktree, causing `update-agent-context.ps1` and other scripts to fail with "directory not found" errors.

## Root Cause
- `.kittify/` is gitignored, so worktrees don't get it automatically
- `create-new-feature.ps1` was only copying `AGENTS.md` and `memory/`, not `templates/`
- Migration script only handled `AGENTS.md` symlinks, not `templates/`

## Solution

**PowerShell Script** (`create-new-feature.ps1`):
- Added templates/ directory copy after worktree creation
- Follows same pattern as AGENTS.md and memory/ copies
- Uses `-Force` and `-Recurse` flags for reliability

**Migration Script** (`m_0_8_0_worktree_agents_symlink.py`):
- Extended to create/symlink both `AGENTS.md` and `templates/`
- Each resource is optional (backward compatible)
- Proper fallback: symlinks on Unix, copies on Windows if symlink fails
- Handles broken symlinks and existing directories
- Comprehensive error handling and dry-run support

## Testing
- ✅ Verified templates/ copied to new worktrees
- ✅ Migration detects missing templates in existing worktrees
- ✅ Migration creates symlinks (or copies on Windows)
- ✅ Scripts run successfully in worktrees

## Impact
- **Severity**: CRITICAL (breaks worktree workflow on Windows)
- **Scope**: All Windows users using worktrees
- **Risk**: Low (additive change, backward compatible)

author: fronc
body:
# Allow Admin/Owner to Opt Out of Auto-Approval

## Summary

This PR implements an option for admin and owner accounts to disable auto-approval of their own requests, addressing a long-standing feature request. Admin requests can now go through the normal pending → approved flow, enabling integration with third-party tools and manual queue management.

**Closes #3926**

---

## Problem

Currently, any request made by an admin or owner account is automatically approved and begins processing immediately. This behavior:

1. **Prevents wishlist functionality** - Admins cannot maintain a queue of desired media
2. **Breaks third-party tool integration** - Tools that intercept pending requests (for availability checking, approval workflows, etc.) cannot process admin requests
3. **Limits admin flexibility** - Features are more restricted on accounts with greater permissions

---

## Solution

Modified the permission system to treat auto-approve permissions explicitly for admin users, rather than granting them implicitly via the admin role.

### Key Changes

1. **`server/lib/permissions.ts`**
   - Added `isAutoApprovePermission()` helper function
   - Modified `hasPermission()` to NOT bypass auto-approve permission checks for admin users
   - Preserved admin bypass for all other permission types
   - Restored `permissions === 0` early return for `isAuthenticated()` with no args

2. **`server/entity/MediaRequest.ts`**
   - Removed `Permission.MANAGE_REQUESTS` from auto-approval status check
   - Admin requests now go to PENDING unless explicit auto-approve permissions are set

3. **`server/routes/user/usersettings.ts`**
   - Added special handling for owner (ID 1) to modify their own auto-approve permissions
   - Protected all other permissions from self-modification

4. **Frontend Components**
   - Updated `PermissionOption` to allow owner to toggle auto-approve in UI
   - Updated request modals to accurately reflect auto-approval status

---

## Permission Behavior Matrix

| Permission Type | Admin Bypass? | Reason |
|-----------------|---------------|--------|
| `MANAGE_*` (Users, Requests, Issues) | ✅ Yes | Administrative functions |
| `REQUEST*`, `VIEW*`, `CREATE*` | ✅ Yes | Standard permissions |
| `AUTO_APPROVE*` | ❌ **No** | Must be explicitly granted |
| `AUTO_REQUEST*` | ✅ Yes | Watchlist sync permissions |

---

## How to Use

### For Admins Who Want Pending Requests

1. Go to **Settings → Users → [Your User] → Permissions**
2. **Uncheck** the auto-approve permissions:
   - Auto-Approve
   - Auto-Approve Movies
   - Auto-Approve Series
   - (And 4K variants if applicable)
3. Save changes

New requests will now go to **Pending** status instead of being automatically approved.

### For Admins Who Want Original Behavior

No action needed. Ensure auto-approve permissions remain checked (they are granted by default for new admin accounts).

---

## Testing Performed

### Functional Tests

- [x] Non-admin users can log in (`/auth/me` returns 200)
- [x] Admin users can log in
- [x] Admin with auto-approve disabled → requests go to PENDING
- [x] Admin with auto-approve enabled → requests auto-approve
- [x] Admin can still approve/reject other users' requests
- [x] Admin can still manage users, settings, issues
- [x] Owner can toggle auto-approve permissions in UI
- [x] Owner cannot modify other permissions on themselves
- [x] Notifications still work for admins

### Edge Cases Verified

- [x] `hasPermission(0, ...)` returns `true` (any logged-in user)
- [x] `hasPermission([], ...)` returns `true` (empty array)
- [x] `hasPermission([AUTO_APPROVE], ...)` requires explicit bit for admin
- [x] `hasPermission([MANAGE_REQUESTS], ...)` allows admin bypass

---

## Comprehensive Permission Audit

All permission behaviors preserved with one intentional change:

| Scenario | Expected | Verified |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Non-admin login | Works | ✅ |
| Admin login | Works | ✅ |
| Admin creates request | Goes to PENDING (if auto-approve disabled) | ✅ |
| Admin approves others' requests | Works | ✅ |
| Admin manages users | Works | ✅ |
| Owner edits auto-approve | Can toggle | ✅ |
| Owner edits other permissions | Blocked | ✅ |
| Non-owner edits owner | Blocked | ✅ |

---

## Breaking Changes

None. This is backwards-compatible:
- Existing admin accounts retain their current permissions
- Auto-approve behavior unchanged unless explicitly modified by user
- All administrative functions continue to work

This change implements a unified visual tokenizer (`UniTok` / VQ-VAE) to enable "native" discrete image tokens in NanoChat, fulfilling the goal of making image tokens first-class citizens alongside text.

Key components:
1.  **`nanochat/unitok.py`**: Contains the VQ-VAE architecture (Encoder, Decoder, Quantizer), Discriminator (PatchGAN), and VQLoss (LPIPS + GAN).
2.  **`scripts/train_visual_tokenizer.py`**: A dedicated training script for the tokenizer.
3.  **`scripts/prepare_vision_data.py`**: A utility to prepare image datasets (like ImageNet or CIFAR) into the Parquet format required by the training script.
4.  **Integration**: Updated `GPTConfig` in `nanochat/gpt.py` to include configuration for visual tokens, preparing the way for full model integration.

author: kevalyq
body:
## Summary
Implements hierarchical Merkle tree batching for activity logs with security Level 2 (Enhanced) and Level 3 (Maximum) as defined in ADR-010 Phase 2.

Fixes #389
Part of #385 (Activity Logging & Integrity Epic)

## Implementation Details

### Core Changes
- **BuildMerkleTreeBatch Job** (226 lines): Hourly scheduled job that batches unbatched Level 2+3 logs into Merkle trees per tenant
  - Handles perfect binary trees (2^n leaves) and odd-numbered leaves (duplicate last)
  - Generates hierarchical Merkle proofs with sibling hashes and positions
  - Dispatches `SubmitMerkleRootToOpenTimestamp` for Level 3 logs (stub for PR-6)
  
- **Activity Model Extensions**:
  - `getSecurityLevels()`: Static method returning log_name → security level mappings
  - `verifyMerkleProof()`: Real implementation replacing stub - iterates proof siblings, hashes left/right, compares to root

- **SubmitMerkleRootToOpenTimestamp Job** (68 lines): Stub for Issue #391 (PR-6) - placeholder for OpenTimestamp integration

- **Scheduler**: Hourly BuildMerkleTreeBatch execution in `routes/console.php`

### Test Coverage
- **10 comprehensive tests** in `BuildMerkleTreeBatchTest.php` (285 lines, 43 assertions):
  - Perfect binary tree (4 leaves)
  - Odd-numbered tree (3 leaves with duplication)
  - Merkle proof verification after batching
  - Deterministic root calculation
  - Level 1 exclusion (Basic security, no Merkle tree)
  - Multi-tenant isolation
  - Already-batched logs skip
  - Empty tenant handling
  - Level 3 OpenTimestamp dispatch (Queue::fake)
  - Level 2 NO OpenTimestamp dispatch

- **Updated ActivityLogTest**: Changed Merkle proof test to use real BuildMerkleTreeBatch integration instead of manual construction

### Quality Gates
✅ **Laravel Pint**: PSR-12 compliant (365 files, 3 issues auto-fixed)
✅ **PHPStan Level Max**: No errors (241 files analyzed)
✅ **Tests**: 1540 passed (4500 assertions) - includes 10 new Merkle tree tests
✅ **REUSE Compliance**: 461/461 files with copyright and license information

### Architecture Compliance
- **SOLID**: Single responsibility (BuildMerkleTreeBatch = build trees only)
- **DRY**: Extends existing Activity model, no duplication
- **KISS**: Standard SHA256 Merkle tree algorithm
- **YAGNI**: Only #389 implementation, #391 OpenTimestamp stubbed for next PR
- **TDD**: Tests written FIRST (BuildMerkleTreeBatchTest before implementation)

### Security Level Behavior
| Log Type | Level | Hash Chain | Merkle Tree | OpenTimestamp | Retention |
|----------|-------|------------|-------------|---------------|-----------|
| default, employee_changes, shift_management | 1 | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | 1 year |
| authentication, rbac_changes, security, scope_changes, customer_changes, site_management | 2 | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | 3 years |
| hr_access, contract_change, works_council_access, guard_book_event, sensitive_access | 3 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (stub) | 7-10 years |

### Next Steps (PR-6: Issue #391)
After this PR is merged:
1. Install `opentimestamps/php-opentimestamps` library
2. Implement `SubmitMerkleRootToOpenTimestamp` job (replace stub)
3. Implement `UpgradeOpenTimestampProofs` job (periodic verification)
4. Add OpenTimestamp calendar configuration
5. Test Level 3 end-to-end with real OTS proof

### References
- ADR-010: Activity Logging & Integrity Mechanisms (3-tier security)
- ADR-002: Tenant Isolation (multi-tenant separation enforced)
- Epic #385: Activity Logging & Integrity (Phase 2: Merkle Trees)
- Issue #389: Implement Merkle Tree Batching (this PR)
- Issue #391: OpenTimestamp Integration (next PR)

author: jkomoros
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes CLI-created spaces that were missing the `defaultPattern` wiring, which broke `wish('#mentionable')` and `wish('#default')` in patterns like `chatbot.tsx` and `note.tsx`.

- CLI space creation now initializes `defaultPattern` (default-app.tsx or home.tsx) identically to Shell-created spaces
- Added mutex-based race protection to prevent duplicate pattern creation when multiple CLI operations run concurrently
- Graceful degradation ensures charm operations continue even if pattern initialization fails
- Better error messages in `wish()` when defaultPattern issues occur

## Root Cause

When the Shell creates a space, it calls `PatternFactory.getOrCreate()` which:
1. Creates the default pattern charm (default-app.tsx for regular spaces, home.tsx for home spaces)
2. Links it to the space cell via `CharmManager.linkDefaultPattern()`

The CLI never did this - it only created user charms directly. This meant:
- `spaceCell.defaultPattern` was undefined
- `wish("#mentionable")` resolved to `spaceCell.defaultPattern.backlinksIndex.mentionable` - which failed silently
- `wish("#default")` also failed

The issue was introduced ~2 months ago when the space cell architecture was established. Any pattern using these wish targets in CLI-created spaces would fail:
- `packages/patterns/chatbot.tsx` (uses `wish("#mentionable")`)
- `packages/patterns/note.tsx` (uses `wish("#mentionable")`)
- Any pattern using `wish("#default")`

## Solution Design

We added `ensureDefaultPattern()` to `CharmsController` rather than `CharmManager` because:

**Architecture decision**: CharmsController is the operations/lifecycle layer that orchestrates complex multi-step processes. CharmManager is the lower-level state management layer.

**Dependency constraints**: `ensureDefaultPattern()` needs `HttpProgramResolver` from `@commontools/js-compiler` to fetch pattern source code. CharmManager can't depend on js-compiler without creating circular package dependencies, but CharmsController already has this dependency.

## Implementation Details

### Race Condition Prevention
Uses mutex-based synchronization with the `editWithRetry` pattern:
- 10-second mutex timeout to handle crashed processes
- 3 retry attempts with 500ms delay
- Double-check after acquiring mutex to prevent TOCTOU issues
- Validates existing pattern isn't a dangling reference to deleted charm

### Error Recovery
All CLI entry points wrap `ensureDefaultPattern()` in try-catch:
- `newCharm()` - warns but continues if pattern init fails
- `linkCharms()` - warns but continues
- `callCharmHandler()` - warns but continues

### wish() Improvements
Returns proper error state `{ error, [UI]: errorUI }` instead of undefined when defaultPattern resolution fails.

## Files Changed

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `packages/charm/src/ops/charms-controller.ts` | Added `ensureDefaultPattern()` with mutex protection |
| `packages/cli/lib/charm.ts` | CLI functions call `ensureDefaultPattern()` with graceful degradation |
| `packages/runner/src/builtins/wish.ts` | Better error handling for defaultPattern failures |
| `packages/charm/test/ensure-default-pattern.test.ts` | New unit tests |

## Test plan

- [x] **CLI creates defaultPattern**: `ct charm new` in fresh space creates DefaultCharmList automatically
- [x] **wish('#mentionable') works**: Deployed chatbot.tsx in CLI-created space, mentionables resolved correctly
- [x] **Race condition prevention**: 3 concurrent `ct charm new` calls created only 1 DefaultCharmList
- [x] **Playwright browser test**: CLI-created space works correctly in Shell UI
- [x] **All charm tests pass**: `deno test packages/charm/test/`
- [x] **Lint/format clean**: `deno fmt` and `deno lint` pass

Fixes [CT-1133](https://linear.app/common-tools/issue/CT-1133)

author: sharkfinpro
body:
This pull request introduces improvements to how the application handles window content scaling, ensuring that UI elements and rendering adapt dynamically to DPI and monitor scaling changes. The most significant updates include tracking the content scale factor, updating ImGui and renderer settings when the scale changes, and providing a mechanism to flag the UI for updates. These changes enhance UI consistency and rendering correctness on high-DPI displays.

**Content Scaling and DPI Awareness:**

* Added tracking of the window's content scale (`m_contentScale`) in the `Window` class, with a getter method (`getContentScale`) to access it. The content scale is now initialized and updated whenever the window's DPI scaling changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-73fb86b407cf5de3db24fba4d87b42f0dfe43e8a9796dfbe904e8e314df32da6R130-R143) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a12780584fc1f760e03e1ffbfcfd4f2b02630cc4d09c644772be6302b046539dR66-R67)
* Registered a new GLFW window content scale callback (`contentScaleCallback`) that updates ImGui's style and font scaling, updates the internal scale state, and flags the ImGui dock for updates when the content scale changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-73fb86b407cf5de3db24fba4d87b42f0dfe43e8a9796dfbe904e8e314df32da6R52-R53) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-73fb86b407cf5de3db24fba4d87b42f0dfe43e8a9796dfbe904e8e314df32da6R156-R168) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a12780584fc1f760e03e1ffbfcfd4f2b02630cc4d09c644772be6302b046539dL36-R47)

**ImGui Integration Enhancements:**

* Modified `initImGui` in the `Window` class to be non-const, allowing it to update the internal content scale state during initialization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-73fb86b407cf5de3db24fba4d87b42f0dfe43e8a9796dfbe904e8e314df32da6L116-R121) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a12780584fc1f760e03e1ffbfcfd4f2b02630cc4d09c644772be6302b046539dL36-R47)
* Added a `markDockNeedsUpdate` method to `ImGuiInstance` to allow external triggers (such as a DPI change) to signal that the ImGui dock layout should be refreshed. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-08fae2ed4c1332d7decde8a9a2236ddd1e85b882ecd6282edf3f4a30c92de829R231-R235) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-498c2b7bedee709dc27307e81d1dfb1aa2db29f12a3926c78ace450867c2fdf2R47-R48)

**Rendering Adjustments for Content Scale:**

* Updated rendering logic in `RenderingManager` so that 2D renderer extents are divided by the current content scale, ensuring correct sizing and positioning of rendered elements after DPI changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-def7951aba553f067fb3b24a9973128c6673a4d9d66a68c865a23749d7611129L256-R259) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-def7951aba553f067fb3b24a9973128c6673a4d9d66a68c865a23749d7611129L285-R294)

**Window Initialization Improvements:**

* Enabled `GLFW_SCALE_TO_MONITOR` during window creation to ensure the application receives accurate DPI scaling information from the OS.

**Dependency and Include Updates:**

* Included the `ImGuiInstance.h` header in `Window.cpp` to support direct interaction with ImGui from the windowing system.

1. Stack trace showed `app_database.g.dart:952` - Drift's generated code failed when mapping NULL values

**Solution Applied (Commits: e7892dd, 9fc8e20):**

   - Added `.withDefault(const Constant(''))` to ALL required text columns in Events table
   - Added `.withDefault(const Constant(0))` to integer columns

   - Replaced `TableMigration` with custom SQL migration
   - Uses `COALESCE(column, default_value)` to provide defaults when copying NULL values
   - Creates new table → copies data with defaults → drops old table → renames new table
   - Handles all edge cases: NULL strings → '', NULL integers → 0, NULL dates preserved

3. Restart the app - migration will run automatically

- ✅ Custom migration with COALESCE safely converts existing NULL data
- ✅ No data loss - all existing events preserved with proper defaults
- ✅ Future inserts automatically use default values for missing fields

## Summary

- Replace custom logging setup that conflicted with uvicorn's logging system in production
- Add `LogConfig` Pydantic model using uvicorn's native formatters (`DefaultFormatter`, `AccessFormatter`)
- Use `dictConfig()` at module load for proper integration with uvicorn
- Remove `SafeFormatter`, `RequestIDFilter`, and `configure_logging()` that were being overridden

## Problem

The previous logging configuration was not working in production because:
1. Custom `configure_logging()` ran at module import time
2. Uvicorn would then reconfigure logging after importing the app
3. Our custom handlers and formatters were being overwritten

## Solution

Use the same pattern as osrsdiff - a `LogConfig` Pydantic model with `dictConfig()` that uses uvicorn's native formatters. This properly integrates with uvicorn's logging infrastructure instead of fighting against it.

This PR implements inline annotations that display `pinyin` and `definitions` directly below saved words in the Study tab, providing visual feedback.

## Changes Made
- Created a `<Word>` component to render individual tokens with inline annotations.
  - This component has the same functionality as `<DemoWord>`, minus the `isSpecialChar` prop which needs to be addressed in an upcoming GH issue.
- Updated StudyTab to use `savedWordsContext` to determine if a word is saved.
- Added styling for the tokenized text layout and inline annotations.
- Annotations automatically show and hide based on word saved status.

## Technical Details:
- Inline annotations display `pinyin` and English definitions.
- Saved words are highlighted with teal color and underlined.

## Demo Video:
Here's a video demonstrating how words will show annotations dynamically when saved, and also hide them when they are deleted.

author: cs121
body:
### Motivation
- Reduce distracting "wandering" of screen-space godrays when the camera rotates while keeping the default physically plausible behavior off by default. 
- Provide configurable smoothing and per-second clamp so both sky-diffuse shafts and sharper light-texture shafts share the same stabilization logic. 
- Ensure stabilization can be reset on large view jumps (teleport/map load/vid_restart) to avoid artifacts after discontinuities. 

### Description
- Added CVars: `r_godrays_stabilize` (0..1, default 0.0), `r_godrays_smooth_rate` (default 8.0), `r_godrays_max_shift` (pixels/sec, default 0.0), and `r_godrays_reset_on_teleport` (default 1) and registered them in `gl_rmisc.c`.
- Implemented a persistent per-view filter `godrays_stabilization_t r_godrays_stabilization` and helper `GL_GetGodraysLightPos` in `gl_rmain.c` that computes exponential smoothing (alpha = 1 - exp(-dt * rate)) and optional max-movement clamping in pixels/sec, plus teleport/angle-jump reset logic.
- Added `R_ResetGodraysStabilization` (declared in `glquake.h`) and call sites on map load and GL init (`R_NewMap` and `GL_Init`), and use the stabilized position when uploading `LightParams` for the godrays shader in `GL_GenerateGodraysTexture`.
- Updated externs/registration and minor plumbing across `Quake/gl_rmain.c`, `Quake/gl_rmisc.c`, `Quake/gl_vidsdl.c`, and `Quake/glquake.h` to integrate the feature and ensure state reset on vid_restart/map changes.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.
- The change is limited to renderer state and shader parameter feeding and is designed to be opt-in with `r_godrays_stabilize` defaulting to off.
